docs.text: Query and write rows ¶ Queries are explicit: nothing runs until you evaluate a query, values are bound parameters, and relations load only when you ask. Examples use the Billing models from Define models . Query rows ¶ Async Sync # inside an async operation or handler invoice = await Invoice . aget ( id = invoice_id ) maybe = await Invoice . aget_or_none ( reference = "INV-7" ) unpaid = await Invoice . filter ( customer_id = customer . id , paid = False ) . order_by ( "reference" ) first = await Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . afirst () count = await Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . acount () page = await Invoice . all () . apaginate ( PageParams ( page = 1 , page_size = 20 )) projected = await Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . order_by ( "reference" ) . aproject ( InvoiceOut ) one_projected = await Invoice . aget_as ( InvoiceOut , id = invoice_id ) maybe_projected = await Invoice . aget_or_none_as ( InvoiceOut , reference = "INV-7" ) # inside a sync handler (runs in the bounded worker pool) invoice = Invoice . get ( id = invoice_id ) maybe = Invoice . get_or_none ( reference = "INV-7" ) unpaid = ( Invoice . filter ( customer_id = customer . id , paid = False ) . order_by ( "reference" ) . list () ) first = Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . first () count = Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . count () page = Invoice . all () . paginate ( PageParams ( page = 1 , page_size = 20 )) projected = Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . order_by ( "reference" ) . project ( InvoiceOut ) one_projected = Invoice . get_as ( InvoiceOut , id = invoice_id ) maybe_projected = Invoice . get_or_none_as ( InvoiceOut , reference = "INV-7" ) PageParams comes from hinoki.pagination . aget and aget_as raise Invoice.NotFound (a 404 in a request) or MultipleObjectsReturned . Building a query ( filter , order_by , limit , offset , select_related , prefetch_related ) issues no SQL; awaiting it or calling an evaluation method does. aproject / project , apaginate_as / paginate_as , aget_as / get_as , and aget_or_none_as / get_or_none_as encode eligible scalar, select_related , and 1-level prefetch_related (reverse foreign keys and many-to-many) schemas directly from Rust rows, materializing Python Schema instances lazily from the owned rows if inspected and falling back transparently when hooks, computed fields, validators, or scoped prefetches are present. A projected item passes isinstance , dataclasses.is_dataclass , dataclasses.asdict , dataclasses.replace and copy.replace as the Schema itself. dataclasses.fields(type(item)) sees no fields (the class of a projected item is not the Schema ); use dataclasses.fields(item) . Query methods ¶ Every read and write entry point has an async form ( a* ) for async def handlers and a matching sync form for def handlers. Starting a query on Model ¶ Method Returns Behavior Model.all() QuerySet[M] All rows (live rows only on @db.soft_delete() models). Model.filter(**conditions) QuerySet[M] Shortcut for Model.all().filter(**conditions) . Model.with_deleted() QuerySet[M] Includes soft-deleted rows on @db.soft_delete() models. Model.only_deleted() QuerySet[M] Only soft-deleted rows on @db.soft_delete() models. Model.aget(**conditions) / Model.get(...) M Fetch exactly one row; raises Model.NotFound or MultipleObjectsReturned . Model.aget_or_none(**conditions) / Model.get_or_none(...) M \| None Fetch one row or None ; still raises MultipleObjectsReturned if more than one matches. Chainable QuerySet methods ¶ These methods return a new QuerySet without touching the database. Method Behavior .filter(**conditions) Add one or more AND conditions ( field=value or field__op=value ). .order_by(*names) Sort ascending ( "issued_at" ) or descending ( "-issued_at" ). Overrides @db.ordered_by . .limit(count) Cap the number of returned rows. .offset(count) Skip the first count rows. .select_related(*names) Load forward foreign-key relations in the same query ( JOIN ). See Relations . .prefetch_related(*names, **scoped) Load forward, reverse, or many-to-many relations in bounded follow-up queries. Many-to-many links accept scoped querysets ( prefetch_related(tags=Tag.filter(...)) ). Evaluating a QuerySet (reads) ¶ Async Sync Returns Behavior await qs qs.list() list[M] Fetch all matching model instances. await qs.afirst() qs.first() M \| None First matching row, or None . await qs.aget() qs.get() M Exactly one matching row; raises Model.NotFound or MultipleObjectsReturned . await qs.acount() qs.count() int Count matching rows (ignores order_by ). await qs.aexists() qs.exists() bool True if at least one row matches. await qs.aproject(Schema) qs.project(Schema) list[S] Project matching rows to a Schema via the lazy Rust row path when eligible. await qs.apaginate(params=None, *, concurrent=False) qs.paginate(...) Page[M] Offset page plus total . concurrent=True runs rows and count concurrently outside a transaction. await qs.apaginate_as(Schema, params=None, *, concurrent=False) qs.paginate_as(...) Page[S] Offset page projected to Schema via the lazy Rust row path. await qs.apaginate_cursor(params) qs.paginate_cursor(params) CursorPage[M] Keyset page using a signed cursor, with no COUNT query. apaginate runs the count and the page as two statements; concurrent writes can make total and items disagree slightly. apaginate_cursor runs one statement and no count; see cursor pagination . @db.ordered_by applies only when a query has no order_by . Counts and bulk updates ignore it. Write and soft-delete methods ¶ Async Sync Target Behavior Model.acreate(data=None, /, *, returning=True, **values) Model.create(...) Model Insert one row from a Schema and/or server keywords. row.asave() row.save() instance Persist changed columns on an existing instance. row.aupdate_from(data=None, /, **values) row.update_from(...) instance Apply a Schema / keywords and save changed columns. Model.aupdate(*, returning=True, **values) Model.update(...) Model Update one row by primary key; raises NotFound if missing ( returning=True ). Model.aupdate_where(conditions, values, *, returning=True) Model.update_where(...) Model Conditional UPDATE matching conditions (supports field__op ). qs.aupdate(values, *, returning=True) qs.update(...) QuerySet Update all matching rows (refuses limit / offset ). Model.adelete(**conditions) / qs.adelete() delete(...) Model / QuerySet Delete matching rows (sets delete timestamp on @db.soft_delete() models). row.asoft_delete() row.soft_delete() instance Soft-delete one @db.soft_delete() instance. row.arestore() / qs.arestore() restore() instance / QuerySet Clear the soft-delete timestamp ( Model.only_deleted().filter(...).arestore() ). row.ahard_delete() / qs.ahard_delete() hard_delete() instance / QuerySet Physical SQL DELETE on a @db.soft_delete() model. Model.abulk_create(items, *, returning=True) Model.bulk_create(...) Model Insert many Schema objects or dicts in one transaction/savepoint. Model.abulk_update(instances) Model.bulk_update(...) Model Save changed instances in one transaction/savepoint. Model.abulk_delete(items) Model.bulk_delete(...) Model Delete instances or primary keys in chunks of up to 10 000. Filter operators ¶ filter(field=value) and filter(field__op=value) accept model field names and a fixed set of lookup operators compiled in Rust. Every condition in a filter(...) call (or chained .filter(...).filter(...) ) is combined with AND , values are bound parameters, and SQL identifiers come from model metadata. Lookup Example Compiled SQL Notes (exact) paid=False paid = $1 Passing None ( voided_at=None ) compiles to IS NULL . ne status__ne="draft" status <> $1 Passing None compiles to IS NOT NULL . For non- None values, NULL rows do not match. gt total__gt=100 total > $1 Rejects None ( FieldError ). gte total__gte=100 total >= $1 Rejects None ( FieldError ). lt total__lt=500 total < $1 Rejects None ( FieldError ). lte total__lte=500 total <= $1 Rejects None ( FieldError ). in status__in=["open", "overdue"] status IN ($1, $2) Takes a sequence/set; rejects str and bytes ( FieldError ) so strings are never split by character. isnull voided_at__isnull=True voided_at IS NULL False compiles to IS NOT NULL . contains reference__contains="inv-" case-insensitive LIKE Escapes % , _ and \ literally. Rejected on Decimal columns ( FieldError ). field__ne=value compiles to <> : rows where the column is NULL are not returned. Add an isnull filter when they matter. contains matches text case-insensitively and treats % , _ and \ literally. SQLite folds ASCII case only; MySQL and MariaDB assume the NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES mode is off (the default). Passing None with any operator other than exact equality or ne raises FieldError . Filtering across relations ¶ Forward foreign keys : traverse a foreign-key relation with __ and any operator above: invoices = await Invoice . filter ( customer__name__contains = "acme" , paid = False ) Hinoki adds the required JOIN automatically and matches only live rows when the target model uses @db.soft_delete() . * Many-to-many links : filter on a target field ( tags__slug="rust" ) or test whether any live link exists ( tags__isnull=True / False ): rust_posts = await Post . filter ( tags__slug = "rust" ) untagged = await Post . filter ( tags__isnull = True ) Many-to-many filters compile to a subquery against the bridge table and ignore soft-deleted targets. <link>__isnull cannot be combined with other conditions on the same link. * Reverse foreign keys : filtering from the parent across a reverse relation raises FieldError ; query the child model directly instead. Client query filters ( FilterSet ) ¶ For generated CRUD list endpoints, declare accepted HTTP query parameters with FilterSet from hinoki.filters instead of passing raw query parameters to filter() . Only declared fields and shapes are accepted; validation and query compilation run in Rust. Declaration Query string Behavior paid: Eq[bool] ?paid=false Exact match ( = ). status: In[Literal["open", "paid"]] ?status=open,paid Membership ( IN , up to 50 comma-separated values). issued: Range[date] ?issued.from=2026-01-01&issued.to=2026-01-31 Inclusive bounds ( >= / <= ); either end is optional ( Bounds[T] ). search = Search("reference", "notes") ?search=inv Case-insensitive contains matching any listed text column. ordering = ("issued", "reference") ?ordering=-issued Allowed sort columns; prefix - for descending. Supported scalar types for Eq , In , and Range are bool , int , float , str , Literal["..."] , UUID , date , datetime , and Decimal (optionally nullable with | None ). See Generate CRUD routes for full FilterSet usage. Reusable queries ¶ A reusable query is a typed class method returning a QuerySet . There is no hidden manager: Model.all() means every live row on a soft-delete model and every row on an ordinary model. # notes/apps/billing/models.py (continued) from typing import Self from hinoki.orm import QuerySet class Invoice ( Model ): ... # fields as in Define models voided_at : datetime | None = None @classmethod def open ( cls ) -> QuerySet [ Self ]: return cls . filter ( voided_at = None , paid = False ) Pass it where the framework asks for a base query, so every operation sees the same rows: # notes/apps/billing/api.py from typing import Any from hinoki import API , Caller , crud from hinoki.admin import ModelAdmin from hinoki.filters import Eq , FilterSet from hinoki.orm import QuerySet from notes.security import billing_staff from .models import Invoice from .schemas import InvoiceOut class InvoiceFilters ( FilterSet ): paid : Eq [ bool ] @crud ( Invoice , path = "/invoices" , read = InvoiceOut , access = billing_staff , filters = InvoiceFilters , ) class Invoices ( API ): def get_queryset ( self , principal : Caller [ Any ] | None ) -> QuerySet [ Invoice ]: return Invoice . open () class InvoiceAdmin ( ModelAdmin [ Invoice ]): def queryset ( self , principal : Caller [ Any ]) -> QuerySet [ Invoice ]: return Invoice . open () Rule Where row order @db.ordered_by(...) ( model options ) an app-wide policy, such as hiding voided rows a named class method, used in get_queryset() and ModelAdmin.queryset() rows that depend on the caller get_queryset(principal) or ModelAdmin.queryset(principal) Not a security boundary Model.all() and raw SQL skip a reusable query. Keep ownership and permissions in access= , owner= and ModelAdmin.can() . Create and update ¶ # inside an async operation invoice = await Invoice . acreate ( InvoiceIn ( reference = "INV-8" ), customer_id = customer . id ) invoice . paid = True await invoice . asave () # updates the changed columns await invoice . aupdate_from ( InvoicePatch ( paid = False )) changed = await Invoice . aupdate_where ({ "id" : invoice . id , "paid" : False }, { "paid" : True }) Keywords set by the server win over values from a Schema ; a Schema never carries the primary key. asave() writes changed columns and refuses a primary-key change. aupdate_where(conditions, values) puts ownership and state checks in the SQL condition: use it for conditional writes instead of read-then-write. QuerySet.aupdate(values) and adelete() act on every matching row, ignore ordering and refuse a query with limit or offset ; select the keys first and filter on id__in=[...] . On a model decorated with @db.soft_delete() , adelete() / delete() sets the delete timestamp with a scoped UPDATE ; use arestore() / restore() to clear it, and ahard_delete() / hard_delete() for a physical DELETE . Model queries are live-only by default; Model.with_deleted() and Model.only_deleted() are explicit class-level scopes. Relations use the live scope too: reverse relations, many-to-many links, and forward select_related / prefetch_related , where a referenced soft-deleted row reads as None . A filter across a relation ( parent__name=... ) joins live rows only. For @db.track_status() , instance saves bump changed_at only when the value actually changes. Bulk QuerySet.aupdate() cannot compare stored values and bumps the timestamp whenever the tracked field appears in values , including when it equals the stored value. Writing many rows at once ¶ abulk_create , abulk_update and abulk_delete (sync bulk_* ) each run in one transaction, or a savepoint inside an open one: # inside an async operation rows = await Invoice . abulk_create ( [ { "reference" : "A-1" , "customer_id" : customer . id }, { "reference" : "A-2" , "customer_id" : customer . id }, ] ) rows [ 0 ] . paid = True await Invoice . abulk_update ( rows ) # saves changed rows only deleted = await Invoice . abulk_delete ([ rows [ 0 ], rows [ 1 ] . id ]) # instances or keys abulk_create takes Schema objects or dicts, each carrying every required value, and returns the rows in order; defaults, factories, validation and hooks apply as for acreate . It takes no server keywords: put them in each item. abulk_update refuses an unsaved instance and returns every instance it was given, unchanged ones included; abulk_delete returns how many rows existed, deletes in chunks of at most 10 000 keys and runs no hooks. One statement per row (per chunk for deletes): these give atomicity, not a batching speed-up. PostgreSQL and SQLite count matched rows; MySQL and MariaDB count rows whose values changed. A model cannot declare a field named returning . docs.text: Queries are explicit: nothing runs until you evaluate a query, values are bound parameters, and relations load only when you ask. Examples use the Billing models from Define models .

docs.text: Async Sync # inside an async operation or handler invoice = await Invoice . aget ( id = invoice_id ) maybe = await Invoice . aget_or_none ( reference = "INV-7" ) unpaid = await Invoice . filter ( customer_id = customer . id , paid = False ) . order_by ( "reference" ) first = await Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . afirst () count = await Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . acount () page = await Invoice . all () . apaginate ( PageParams ( page = 1 , page_size = 20 )) projected = await Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . order_by ( "reference" ) . aproject ( InvoiceOut ) one_projected = await Invoice . aget_as ( InvoiceOut , id = invoice_id ) maybe_projected = await Invoice . aget_or_none_as ( InvoiceOut , reference = "INV-7" ) # inside a sync handler (runs in the bounded worker pool) invoice = Invoice . get ( id = invoice_id ) maybe = Invoice . get_or_none ( reference = "INV-7" ) unpaid = ( Invoice . filter ( customer_id = customer . id , paid = False ) . order_by ( "reference" ) . list () ) first = Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . first () count = Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . count () page = Invoice . all () . paginate ( PageParams ( page = 1 , page_size = 20 )) projected = Invoice . filter ( paid = False ) . order_by ( "reference" ) . project ( InvoiceOut ) one_projected = Invoice . get_as ( InvoiceOut , id = invoice_id ) maybe_projected = Invoice . get_or_none_as ( InvoiceOut , reference = "INV-7" ) PageParams comes from hinoki.pagination . aget and aget_as raise Invoice.NotFound (a 404 in a request) or MultipleObjectsReturned . Building a query ( filter , order_by , limit , offset , select_related , prefetch_related ) issues no SQL; awaiting it or calling an evaluation method does. aproject / project , apaginate_as / paginate_as , aget_as / get_as , and aget_or_none_as / get_or_none_as encode eligible scalar, select_related , and 1-level prefetch_related (reverse foreign keys and many-to-many) schemas directly from Rust rows, materializing Python Schema instances lazily from the owned rows if inspected and falling back transparently when hooks, computed fields, validators, or scoped prefetches are present. A projected item passes isinstance , dataclasses.is_dataclass , dataclasses.asdict , dataclasses.replace and copy.replace as the Schema itself. dataclasses.fields(type(item)) sees no fields (the class of a projected item is not the Schema ); use dataclasses.fields(item) .

docs.text: Every read and write entry point has an async form ( a* ) for async def handlers and a matching sync form for def handlers.

docs.text: Method Returns Behavior Model.all() QuerySet[M] All rows (live rows only on @db.soft_delete() models). Model.filter(**conditions) QuerySet[M] Shortcut for Model.all().filter(**conditions) . Model.with_deleted() QuerySet[M] Includes soft-deleted rows on @db.soft_delete() models. Model.only_deleted() QuerySet[M] Only soft-deleted rows on @db.soft_delete() models. Model.aget(**conditions) / Model.get(...) M Fetch exactly one row; raises Model.NotFound or MultipleObjectsReturned . Model.aget_or_none(**conditions) / Model.get_or_none(...) M \| None Fetch one row or None ; still raises MultipleObjectsReturned if more than one matches.
docs.title: Starting a query on Model

docs.text: These methods return a new QuerySet without touching the database. Method Behavior .filter(**conditions) Add one or more AND conditions ( field=value or field__op=value ). .order_by(*names) Sort ascending ( "issued_at" ) or descending ( "-issued_at" ). Overrides @db.ordered_by . .limit(count) Cap the number of returned rows. .offset(count) Skip the first count rows. .select_related(*names) Load forward foreign-key relations in the same query ( JOIN ). See Relations . .prefetch_related(*names, **scoped) Load forward, reverse, or many-to-many relations in bounded follow-up queries. Many-to-many links accept scoped querysets ( prefetch_related(tags=Tag.filter(...)) ).
docs.title: Chainable QuerySet methods

docs.text: Async Sync Returns Behavior await qs qs.list() list[M] Fetch all matching model instances. await qs.afirst() qs.first() M \| None First matching row, or None . await qs.aget() qs.get() M Exactly one matching row; raises Model.NotFound or MultipleObjectsReturned . await qs.acount() qs.count() int Count matching rows (ignores order_by ). await qs.aexists() qs.exists() bool True if at least one row matches. await qs.aproject(Schema) qs.project(Schema) list[S] Project matching rows to a Schema via the lazy Rust row path when eligible. await qs.apaginate(params=None, *, concurrent=False) qs.paginate(...) Page[M] Offset page plus total . concurrent=True runs rows and count concurrently outside a transaction. await qs.apaginate_as(Schema, params=None, *, concurrent=False) qs.paginate_as(...) Page[S] Offset page projected to Schema via the lazy Rust row path. await qs.apaginate_cursor(params) qs.paginate_cursor(params) CursorPage[M] Keyset page using a signed cursor, with no COUNT query. apaginate runs the count and the page as two statements; concurrent writes can make total and items disagree slightly. apaginate_cursor runs one statement and no count; see cursor pagination . @db.ordered_by applies only when a query has no order_by . Counts and bulk updates ignore it.

docs.text: Async Sync Target Behavior Model.acreate(data=None, /, *, returning=True, **values) Model.create(...) Model Insert one row from a Schema and/or server keywords. row.asave() row.save() instance Persist changed columns on an existing instance. row.aupdate_from(data=None, /, **values) row.update_from(...) instance Apply a Schema / keywords and save changed columns. Model.aupdate(*, returning=True, **values) Model.update(...) Model Update one row by primary key; raises NotFound if missing ( returning=True ). Model.aupdate_where(conditions, values, *, returning=True) Model.update_where(...) Model Conditional UPDATE matching conditions (supports field__op ). qs.aupdate(values, *, returning=True) qs.update(...) QuerySet Update all matching rows (refuses limit / offset ). Model.adelete(**conditions) / qs.adelete() delete(...) Model / QuerySet Delete matching rows (sets delete timestamp on @db.soft_delete() models). row.asoft_delete() row.soft_delete() instance Soft-delete one @db.soft_delete() instance. row.arestore() / qs.arestore() restore() instance / QuerySet Clear the soft-delete timestamp ( Model.only_deleted().filter(...).arestore() ). row.ahard_delete() / qs.ahard_delete() hard_delete() instance / QuerySet Physical SQL DELETE on a @db.soft_delete() model. Model.abulk_create(items, *, returning=True) Model.bulk_create(...) Model Insert many Schema objects or dicts in one transaction/savepoint. Model.abulk_update(instances) Model.bulk_update(...) Model Save changed instances in one transaction/savepoint. Model.abulk_delete(items) Model.bulk_delete(...) Model Delete instances or primary keys in chunks of up to 10 000.

docs.text: filter(field=value) and filter(field__op=value) accept model field names and a fixed set of lookup operators compiled in Rust. Every condition in a filter(...) call (or chained .filter(...).filter(...) ) is combined with AND , values are bound parameters, and SQL identifiers come from model metadata. Lookup Example Compiled SQL Notes (exact) paid=False paid = $1 Passing None ( voided_at=None ) compiles to IS NULL . ne status__ne="draft" status <> $1 Passing None compiles to IS NOT NULL . For non- None values, NULL rows do not match. gt total__gt=100 total > $1 Rejects None ( FieldError ). gte total__gte=100 total >= $1 Rejects None ( FieldError ). lt total__lt=500 total < $1 Rejects None ( FieldError ). lte total__lte=500 total <= $1 Rejects None ( FieldError ). in status__in=["open", "overdue"] status IN ($1, $2) Takes a sequence/set; rejects str and bytes ( FieldError ) so strings are never split by character. isnull voided_at__isnull=True voided_at IS NULL False compiles to IS NOT NULL . contains reference__contains="inv-" case-insensitive LIKE Escapes % , _ and \ literally. Rejected on Decimal columns ( FieldError ). field__ne=value compiles to <> : rows where the column is NULL are not returned. Add an isnull filter when they matter. contains matches text case-insensitively and treats % , _ and \ literally. SQLite folds ASCII case only; MySQL and MariaDB assume the NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES mode is off (the default). Passing None with any operator other than exact equality or ne raises FieldError .
docs.title: Filter operators

docs.text: Forward foreign keys : traverse a foreign-key relation with __ and any operator above: invoices = await Invoice . filter ( customer__name__contains = "acme" , paid = False ) Hinoki adds the required JOIN automatically and matches only live rows when the target model uses @db.soft_delete() . * Many-to-many links : filter on a target field ( tags__slug="rust" ) or test whether any live link exists ( tags__isnull=True / False ): rust_posts = await Post . filter ( tags__slug = "rust" ) untagged = await Post . filter ( tags__isnull = True ) Many-to-many filters compile to a subquery against the bridge table and ignore soft-deleted targets. <link>__isnull cannot be combined with other conditions on the same link. * Reverse foreign keys : filtering from the parent across a reverse relation raises FieldError ; query the child model directly instead.
docs.title: Filtering across relations

docs.text: For generated CRUD list endpoints, declare accepted HTTP query parameters with FilterSet from hinoki.filters instead of passing raw query parameters to filter() . Only declared fields and shapes are accepted; validation and query compilation run in Rust. Declaration Query string Behavior paid: Eq[bool] ?paid=false Exact match ( = ). status: In[Literal["open", "paid"]] ?status=open,paid Membership ( IN , up to 50 comma-separated values). issued: Range[date] ?issued.from=2026-01-01&issued.to=2026-01-31 Inclusive bounds ( >= / <= ); either end is optional ( Bounds[T] ). search = Search("reference", "notes") ?search=inv Case-insensitive contains matching any listed text column. ordering = ("issued", "reference") ?ordering=-issued Allowed sort columns; prefix - for descending. Supported scalar types for Eq , In , and Range are bool , int , float , str , Literal["..."] , UUID , date , datetime , and Decimal (optionally nullable with | None ). See Generate CRUD routes for full FilterSet usage.
docs.title: Client query filters (FilterSet)

docs.text: A reusable query is a typed class method returning a QuerySet . There is no hidden manager: Model.all() means every live row on a soft-delete model and every row on an ordinary model. # notes/apps/billing/models.py (continued) from typing import Self from hinoki.orm import QuerySet class Invoice ( Model ): ... # fields as in Define models voided_at : datetime | None = None @classmethod def open ( cls ) -> QuerySet [ Self ]: return cls . filter ( voided_at = None , paid = False ) Pass it where the framework asks for a base query, so every operation sees the same rows: # notes/apps/billing/api.py from typing import Any from hinoki import API , Caller , crud from hinoki.admin import ModelAdmin from hinoki.filters import Eq , FilterSet from hinoki.orm import QuerySet from notes.security import billing_staff from .models import Invoice from .schemas import InvoiceOut class InvoiceFilters ( FilterSet ): paid : Eq [ bool ] @crud ( Invoice , path = "/invoices" , read = InvoiceOut , access = billing_staff , filters = InvoiceFilters , ) class Invoices ( API ): def get_queryset ( self , principal : Caller [ Any ] | None ) -> QuerySet [ Invoice ]: return Invoice . open () class InvoiceAdmin ( ModelAdmin [ Invoice ]): def queryset ( self , principal : Caller [ Any ]) -> QuerySet [ Invoice ]: return Invoice . open () Rule Where row order @db.ordered_by(...) ( model options ) an app-wide policy, such as hiding voided rows a named class method, used in get_queryset() and ModelAdmin.queryset() rows that depend on the caller get_queryset(principal) or ModelAdmin.queryset(principal) Not a security boundary Model.all() and raw SQL skip a reusable query. Keep ownership and permissions in access= , owner= and ModelAdmin.can() .
docs.title: Reusable queries

docs.text: # inside an async operation invoice = await Invoice . acreate ( InvoiceIn ( reference = "INV-8" ), customer_id = customer . id ) invoice . paid = True await invoice . asave () # updates the changed columns await invoice . aupdate_from ( InvoicePatch ( paid = False )) changed = await Invoice . aupdate_where ({ "id" : invoice . id , "paid" : False }, { "paid" : True }) Keywords set by the server win over values from a Schema ; a Schema never carries the primary key. asave() writes changed columns and refuses a primary-key change. aupdate_where(conditions, values) puts ownership and state checks in the SQL condition: use it for conditional writes instead of read-then-write. QuerySet.aupdate(values) and adelete() act on every matching row, ignore ordering and refuse a query with limit or offset ; select the keys first and filter on id__in=[...] . On a model decorated with @db.soft_delete() , adelete() / delete() sets the delete timestamp with a scoped UPDATE ; use arestore() / restore() to clear it, and ahard_delete() / hard_delete() for a physical DELETE . Model queries are live-only by default; Model.with_deleted() and Model.only_deleted() are explicit class-level scopes. Relations use the live scope too: reverse relations, many-to-many links, and forward select_related / prefetch_related , where a referenced soft-deleted row reads as None . A filter across a relation ( parent__name=... ) joins live rows only. For @db.track_status() , instance saves bump changed_at only when the value actually changes. Bulk QuerySet.aupdate() cannot compare stored values and bumps the timestamp whenever the tracked field appears in values , including when it equals the stored value.

docs.text: Quick start ¶ Create a project, run its tests and serve it. Everything runs locally; the database is a SQLite file. Create a project ¶ From the Hinoki checkout: uv run hinoki new hinoki new asks only what it needs. Give these answers and keep the other defaults: Prompt Default Answer Project name notes Parent directory . .. (beside the checkout) Database none sqlite Server kiso kiso Agent instructions and MCP config? yes yes Agent skills? no no Initialize a git repository? yes yes Install dependencies (uv sync)? yes yes Create an app now? yes yes App name core entries It writes the project and the entries app, runs git init and uv sync , and prints the next commands. The files that matter: notes/ ├── hinoki.toml manifest: application, routes and the entries app ├── notes/ │ ├── main.py the application │ ├── api.py GET /health │ ├── routes.py routes = [health] │ ├── settings.py typed settings, NOTES_* variables │ ├── rules.py architecture rules │ └── apps/ │ └── entries/ starter app registered in hinoki.toml │ ├── api.py │ ├── routes.py │ ├── models.py │ └── migrations/ ├── tests/ pytest suite └── AGENTS.md agent instructions The generated project serves /health . The entries app starts with an empty route list and space for its models and migrations. Choosing no at Create an app now? creates just the project. Add another app shows how to add one later. Scripts and CI uv run hinoki new notes --dir .. --no-input --database sqlite --git --install --app entries gives the same answers without prompts. Plain --no-input uses the defaults instead: no database, no git init , no uv sync and no app. All options are in hinoki new . Check and test it ¶ cd ../notes uv run hinoki check uv run pytest hinoki check runs the project's rules (the eight listed in notes/rules.py ) and prints one line for each; a violation names the file, the line and a fix. The test calls /health in process and needs no database. Run both again after every change, as AGENTS.md tells an agent to. Serve it ¶ uv run hinoki dev hinoki dev serves on http://127.0.0.1:8000 and reloads when a file changes. In another terminal: curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health {"status":"ok"} At startup hinoki dev logs a warning that allowed_hosts is '*' : the application answers to any Host header. It is harmless on your machine. To name the hosts you serve, and silence it, add NOTES_ALLOWED_HOSTS=127.0.0.1,localhost to .env ; see allowed_hosts . Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs for the generated OpenAPI UI, or run uv run hinoki routes to inspect the route map that Hinoki(settings=ProjectSettings, ...) loaded automatically from notes/routes.py ( [project] routes in hinoki.toml ): uv run hinoki routes GET /health public notes.api.health What the manifest does ¶ hinoki.toml registers the application, the project's route map ( [project] routes ), the rules it runs and each app's persistence and dependencies. notes/main.py loads [project] routes automatically, while notes/routes.py decides which apps are mounted over HTTP: [project] application = "notes.main:app" routes = "notes.routes:routes" rules = [ "notes.rules:project_rules" ] notes/main.py declares the application: # notes/main.py from hinoki import Hinoki from notes.settings import ProjectSettings app = Hinoki ( settings = ProjectSettings , # NOTES_* variables and .env title = "Notes" , openapi_url = "/openapi.json" , docs_url = "/docs" , ) # routes, rules and middleware come from hinoki.toml Hinoki(settings=ProjectSettings, ...) reads hinoki.toml automatically, loading notes/routes.py ( [project] routes ) and rules , so main.py stays short. Commands read the same manifest, so inside the project they need no module paths. Where the database is configured ¶ Answering sqlite added one field to notes/settings.py : # notes/settings.py from hinoki import settings class ProjectSettings ( settings . AppSettings , prefix = "NOTES_" , dotenv = ".env" ): database : settings . DatabaseSettings With no value set, it is the SQLite file .hinoki/local.sqlite3 . Each field of DatabaseSettings is a NOTES_DATABASE__<FIELD> variable (two underscores between the group and the field), read from the environment or from .env in the project directory. uv run hinoki settings lists every variable and where its value came from. To use another file: # .env NOTES_DATABASE__URL = sqlite://./.hinoki/notes.sqlite3 Configure a database covers PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, and connection fields instead of a URL. The project has no models yet; add them in the app, as the next section and the tutorial show. Your first app ¶ Models live in apps, not in the project package. hinoki new created entries when you answered the last question: notes/apps/entries/ ├── api.py starter for the app’s endpoints ├── routes.py empty app route list ├── models.py starter for the app’s models └── migrations/ migration package It is registered in hinoki.toml : [[apps]] name = "entries" models = "notes.apps.entries.models" migrations = "notes.apps.entries.migrations" requires = [] After adding an endpoint or a group to the app's own route list, mount that list in the project's route map: # notes/routes.py from hinoki import Includable , Mount from notes.api import health from notes.apps.entries.routes import routes as entries_routes routes : list [ Includable ] = [ health , Mount ( "/entries" , entries_routes )] Endpoints inside the app declare paths relative to the /entries prefix. App names are lower-case letters and digits with single underscores between words (for example api_v1 ), starting with a letter. Define the app's models in notes/apps/entries/models.py , then uv run hinoki migrations plan entries ; 9. Projects and apps walks through it. Add another app ¶ If you answered no, or want a second app, create it from the project: uv run hinoki app create billing Next ¶ Tutorial : build an API layer by layer. 9. Projects and apps : add an app with its own models and migrations to this project. Notes example : a separate, complete project with a model, schemas and generated CRUD routes.

docs.text: Models live in apps, not in the project package. hinoki new created entries when you answered the last question: notes/apps/entries/ ├── api.py starter for the app’s endpoints ├── routes.py empty app route list ├── models.py starter for the app’s models └── migrations/ migration package It is registered in hinoki.toml : [[apps]] name = "entries" models = "notes.apps.entries.models" migrations = "notes.apps.entries.migrations" requires = [] After adding an endpoint or a group to the app's own route list, mount that list in the project's route map: # notes/routes.py from hinoki import Includable , Mount from notes.api import health from notes.apps.entries.routes import routes as entries_routes routes : list [ Includable ] = [ health , Mount ( "/entries" , entries_routes )] Endpoints inside the app declare paths relative to the /entries prefix. Define the app's models in notes/apps/entries/models.py , then uv run hinoki migrations plan entries ; 9. Projects and apps walks through it.

docs.text: Relations ¶ A relation is an ordinary foreign-key column. Related rows load only when a query asks for them: attribute access never performs I/O. Declare a foreign key ¶ # notes/apps/billing/models.py from typing import ClassVar from uuid import UUID , uuid4 from hinoki import db from hinoki.orm import Model , OnDelete , Related , field , foreign_key , pk class Customer ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) name : str = field ( max_length = 120 ) invoices : ClassVar [ "Related[list[Invoice]]" ] @db . indexed ( "customer_id" ) class Invoice ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) customer_id : UUID = foreign_key ( Customer , on_delete = OnDelete . RESTRICT , related_name = "invoices" ) reference : str = field ( max_length = 40 , unique = True ) customer : ClassVar [ Related [ Customer ]] customer_id is stored on billing_invoices . invoice.customer is the forward relation (named after the column without _id ); customer.invoices is the reverse relation, created only when related_name is set. The ClassVar[Related[...]] lines are for type checkers. The column type must match the referenced primary key. on_delete is required and takes an OnDelete member: on_delete When the referenced row is deleted OnDelete.RESTRICT the delete is refused while references exist OnDelete.CASCADE referencing rows are deleted too OnDelete.SET_NULL the column becomes NULL ; the field must be \| None OnDelete.NO_ACTION like RESTRICT , checked at the end of the statement A refused delete raises hinoki.db.DatabaseError ( database request failed ), not UniqueViolation , so it is not translated to 409 : check for references first, or register an error handler for it. Text such as on_delete="cascade" , and SET_NULL on a non-nullable field, are refused with RegistrationError at import: # notes/apps/billing/models.py (continued) @db . indexed ( "invoice_id" ) class Payment ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) invoice_id : UUID | None = foreign_key ( Invoice , on_delete = OnDelete . SET_NULL , default = None ) The rule becomes the migration's REFERENCES … ON DELETE clause and the database enforces it. Load related rows ¶ # inside an async operation invoices = await Invoice . all () . select_related ( "customer" ) names = [ invoice . customer . name for invoice in invoices ] customers = await Customer . all () . prefetch_related ( "invoices" ) counts = { c . id : len ( c . invoices ) for c in customers } Method Use for SQL select_related("customer") a forward foreign key (one row) one LEFT JOIN in the same statement prefetch_related("invoices") a reverse or collection relation separate, bounded queries per owner chunk Reading a relation that was not loaded raises RelationNotLoaded . acount() and apaginate() drop a select_related join from their COUNT (a to-one join cannot change the count) but keep a join a filter needs, such as customer__name=... . One-to-one ¶ A one-to-one relation is a foreign key with unique=True : # notes/apps/billing/models.py (continued) class BillingProfile ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) customer_id : UUID = foreign_key ( Customer , on_delete = OnDelete . CASCADE , unique = True , related_name = "profile" ) vat_number : str = field ( max_length = 20 ) customer : ClassVar [ Related [ Customer ]] Add profile: ClassVar["Related[BillingProfile | None]"] to Customer for type checkers. profile.customer has one required target; customer.profile is BillingProfile | None . Load them with select_related("customer") and prefetch_related("profile") . If the database has drifted and holds several rows for one customer, prefetch_related raises MultipleObjectsReturned . The migration creates the foreign key and the unique constraint together. It fails on existing duplicates; clean them up first. Turning an existing foreign key into unique=True rebuilds the table on SQLite and needs a hand-written migration on PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB. Many-to-many ¶ Declare the relation on a model; Hinoki generates and migrates the bridge table ( <owner table>_<name> , one column per side, a composite unique constraint). class Tag ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) name : str = field ( max_length = 40 , unique = True ) class Post ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) title : str = field ( max_length = 80 ) tags : ClassVar [ ManyToMany [ Tag ]] = many_to_many ( Tag , related_name = "posts" , ids_name = "tag_ids" ) # inside an async operation await post . tags . aadd ( red , blue ) # idempotent await post . tags . aset ([ red ], within = Tag . filter ( owner = user )) tags = await post . tags . alist () posts = await Post . filter ( tags__name = "red" ) . prefetch_related ( "tags" ) print ( posts [ 0 ] . tags . loaded , posts [ 0 ] . tag_ids ) # only after prefetch_related aadd , aremove and aset take model instances or keys, run in one transaction that locks the owner row, and refuse more than max_items links ( LinkLimitExceeded ). With within= a key outside that query is treated as missing ( UnknownLinkTarget , a 422 ), and aset replaces only the links inside the scope. ids_name (default <name>_ids ) names the ids field that generated CRUD and derive use ( derive takes it only when only= names it). within is keyword-only on every read and write of the relation, and prefetch_related(tags=queryset) loads only targets in that queryset. The max_items limit applies from both ends. A write through the reverse relation ( tag.posts ) locks the declaring rows it touches that the caller may see (the within= scope applies, so a row outside it is neither locked nor revealed), in key order, and refuses ( LinkLimitExceeded ) a write that would leave one of them past its own max_items , so the limit cannot be raced past from either side; the reverse relation itself holds the library-wide cap. Both ends lock in one order, the declaring rows first and then the owner row, so two writers on opposite ends never wait for each other. A refused write ( LinkLimitExceeded , UnknownLinkTarget ) undoes its own statements in a savepoint, so a handler that catches the error and commits leaves no link behind. Reading links stored beyond max_items (the data broke its bound) raises StoredLinksOverLimit , a server fault ( 500 ), not a validation error. Every write also locks the owner row and re-checks it against the owner scope of generated CRUD and the admin inside that lock, so a row that left the caller's scope reads as missing. The targets a write resolves are held ( FOR KEY SHARE on PostgreSQL, LOCK IN SHARE MODE on MySQL and MariaDB) until the commit, so a target deleted at the same moment either makes the write fail with UnknownLinkTarget or removes the new link with it; on MySQL and MariaDB the reads that decide a write use locking reads, because a transaction there reads one snapshot. SQLite has a single writer. For each chunk of owners, the many-to-many prefetch runs one bounded query from the target table with an inner join to the bridge. It returns one target row per link, so a target shared by owners is repeated in the result. Each statement sees its chunk under the database's transaction isolation; different chunks can observe different states. Rust builds and groups eligible model rows, and Python orchestrates the queries, shares instances across chunks and stores the loaded relations. Custom row builders use the Python fallback. prefetch_related orders targets by the target's default ordering (else its key), with the primary key as the final tie-breaker. NULL sorts before values in ascending order and after values in descending order, including on PostgreSQL. A scoped query may supply an ordering when the model has a default ordering. When the target model is soft-deleting, a deleted target is not linked: reads, filters and prefetches skip it, adding it raises UnknownLinkTarget , it does not count towards max_items , and aset / aremove leave its link alone unless within=Tag.with_deleted() reaches it. A restored target is linked again. bridge="PostTag" adopts a model you wrote instead of generating one (a bridge that is never defined raises RegistrationError at startup, in hinoki check and when planning migrations), and an association model with extra columns stays available as in earlier releases (declare two foreign keys and a composite unique constraint). An association model with its own columns ¶ # notes/apps/billing/models.py (continued) class Tag ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) name : str = field ( max_length = 40 , unique = True ) invoice_links : ClassVar [ "Related[list[InvoiceTag]]" ] @db . unique ( "invoice_id" , "tag_id" ) @db . indexed ( "tag_id" ) class InvoiceTag ( Model ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) invoice_id : UUID = foreign_key ( Invoice , on_delete = OnDelete . CASCADE , related_name = "tag_links" ) tag_id : UUID = foreign_key ( Tag , on_delete = OnDelete . CASCADE , related_name = "invoice_links" ) The composite unique constraint stops duplicate pairs and indexes invoice_id ; @db.indexed("tag_id") indexes the other side. Link and read: # inside an async operation tag = await Tag . acreate ( name = "priority" ) await InvoiceTag . acreate ( invoice_id = invoice . id , tag_id = tag . id ) links = await InvoiceTag . filter ( invoice_id = invoice . id ) . select_related ( "tag" ) tag_names = [ link . tag . name for link in links ] invoice.tag_links holds InvoiceTag rows (load it with prefetch_related("tag_links") ), not Tag objects. The association model can carry its own columns, such as when the tag was added. Foreign keys in abstract models and mixins ¶ A foreign key in an abstract model or mixin is registered once per table model that inherits it. Give the reverse relation a per-model name with the {model} placeholder (the class name in lower case): # notes/apps/billing/models.py (continued) class CustomerOwned ( Model , abstract = True ): customer_id : UUID = foreign_key ( Customer , on_delete = OnDelete . CASCADE , related_name = " {model} _set" ) class CreditNote ( CustomerOwned ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) class Estimate ( CustomerOwned ): id : UUID = pk ( default_factory = uuid4 ) Customer gets creditnote_set and estimate_set . A fixed related_name makes the second inheriting model fail with an error naming both. Without related_name there is no reverse relation. A foreign key cannot reference an abstract model. {model} is the only placeholder. See also ¶ Query and write rows Migrations : foreign-key changes and backend notes

docs.text: Release checklist ¶ How a Hinoki release is prepared. Nothing here runs by itself: the release build workflow produces files, and publishing them is a manual decision of the owner. What a release contains ¶ The PyPI package is named hinoki-api ; the module you import is hinoki ( pip install hinoki-api , import hinoki ). The hinoki name on PyPI belongs to an unrelated project. Artifact Platforms Built by abi3 wheel ( cp312-abi3 ) Linux x86_64 and aarch64 (manylinux 2014), macOS arm64 and x86_64 release-build.yml Source distribution any (needs a Rust toolchain to install) release-build.yml Windows is not built. The native extension uses Unix sockets, so pip install hinoki-api on Windows falls back to the source distribution and stops at a compile error that points to WSL2. On Windows, install and run Hinoki inside WSL2. The release profile uses fat LTO with one codegen unit ( [profile.release] in the workspace Cargo.toml ), which makes the release build slower than a default one. Measure a build before relying on its duration. Before the release ¶ Run the checks of Toolchain and CI on main , including cargo deny check and the full test suite. If the change can affect speed, compare at least five current benchmark samples with a retained baseline (see Benchmarks ). Set the version, which must be the same in pyproject.toml ( project.version ) and in the workspace Cargo.toml ( workspace.package.version ), then run uv lock so uv.lock follows. The docsite footer reads project.version when the site is built, so there is no third place to edit. Apply the compatibility policy : a 0.1.z patch keeps documented contracts and 0.1.0 migration files compatible. A breaking pre-1.0 change requires a later 0.y.0 , release notes and an upgrade path for migration state if version 1 will no longer be read. In CHANGELOG.md , turn Unreleased into [X.Y.Z] - date . Update Status and the Pre-alpha, not released notes in the README if they no longer hold. Merge these changes by pull request. Build and inspect the artifacts ¶ Start Release build on main from the Actions tab ( workflow_dispatch ). A tag that starts with v starts the same workflow. Wait for the four wheel jobs and the sdist job. Each wheel job installs its wheel in a clean Python 3.12 environment and serves a minimal app with scripts/smoke_wheel.py . Download the artifacts and check them locally: gh run download RUN_ID --dir dist uvx twine check dist/*/* Publish ¶ The repository has no automated publishing and no PyPI credentials. Publishing is the owner's action: Upload dist/*/* to PyPI by the owner's chosen method (a project token or trusted publishing configured for this repository). Install the published version in a clean environment and run python scripts/smoke_wheel.py with that environment's interpreter. Tag the release vX.Y.Z . The tag must equal project.version : the release job of deploy-docs.yml checks it and publishes the versioned documentation (see Documentation versions ). The development documentation must be published first. After the release ¶ Create the GitHub release from the tag, with the CHANGELOG.md section as its notes. Open a pull request that adds an empty Unreleased section to CHANGELOG.md .

docs.text: Request lifecycle ¶ The order matters: validation, access and transactions fail in different ways and at different moments. Accept. Kiso accepts the connection, answers what needs no application code and hands the rest to the request pipeline ( Kiso ). With --server granian , Granian calls the ASGI application, which reaches the same pipeline. Route. Hinoki matches the method and path. Authenticate and authorize. For an action with an access policy, the provider resolves a Caller and the policy checks permissions. A rate_limit= policy runs next. The body has not been read yet, so an unauthenticated or rate-limited client cannot make the server buffer it. Bind. Hinoki negotiates the response type from Accept ( 406 when nothing fits), reads the body of POST , PUT , PATCH and QUERY requests, then binds and validates path, query, header and body values. Open the transaction for an atomic=True action. Run the handler , then check its value against the return annotation (a mismatch is 500 internal_error , inside the transaction, unless the action sets validate_response=False ) and render it. A returned Response is neither checked nor rendered. Commit after the response is prepared. An exception or cancellation rolls back before the HTTP error is produced. An unhandled exception never becomes a successful response, and a failed commit is an error. A renderer must not perform hidden database I/O. Limits ¶ Setting Default When exceeded execution.request_timeout 30 s, through response preparation 504 timeout ; an open transaction rolls back execution.max_body_bytes 1 MiB (also each multipart part) 413 payload_too_large execution.max_query_bytes 8 KiB 414 uri_too_long execution.max_header_bytes 32 KiB, names and values combined 431 headers_too_large execution.max_streams 64 open streams per worker 503 with Retry-After: 1 , before the handler runs The size checks run before routing. A sync handler already running when the timeout expires cannot be stopped: it keeps its executor slot until it returns, and its result is discarded. Let the proxy or ASGI server enforce its own request-line and header limits too. Streamed responses ¶ For an action that returns Stream , EventStream or File , everything up to the moment the handler returns the object (access, rate limit, binding, validation, the handler, middleware and request_timeout ) works as for any action, and an error there is the usual JSON answer. Before the handler runs, the worker takes one of its execution.max_streams places, or answers 503 with Retry-After: 1 . The head is then sent, and the body is produced and sent piece by piece: the pieces are not checked against an annotation, a failure can only cut the connection, and the place is given back when the body ends. See stream a response . Request IDs ¶ Each response carries a request ID in server.request_id_header ( x-request-id ), and built-in error JSON repeats it as request_id . Hinoki generates it; with server.trust_request_id=True it accepts a validated inbound ID, only from a trusted proxy. Startup and shutdown ¶ lifecycle.startup_timeout (30 s) and lifecycle.shutdown_timeout (10 s) bound the worker lifespan. A startup failure is reported through the ASGI lifespan protocol; shutdown cleans up resources within its deadline. Startup and shutdown hooks run inside those limits. Where Rust runs ¶ Routing, parsing, validation and selected serialization run in Rust; the server hand-off (Granian and the ASGI adapter, or Kiso's queue) crosses Python objects. See sync and async code for which executor runs what. See also ¶ Transactions Errors Serving
docs.title: Request lifecycle

docs.text: The order matters: validation, access and transactions fail in different ways and at different moments. Accept. Kiso accepts the connection, answers what needs no application code and hands the rest to the request pipeline ( Kiso ). With --server granian , Granian calls the ASGI application, which reaches the same pipeline. Route. Hinoki matches the method and path. Authenticate and authorize. For an action with an access policy, the provider resolves a Caller and the policy checks permissions. A rate_limit= policy runs next. The body has not been read yet, so an unauthenticated or rate-limited client cannot make the server buffer it. Bind. Hinoki negotiates the response type from Accept ( 406 when nothing fits), reads the body of POST , PUT , PATCH and QUERY requests, then binds and validates path, query, header and body values. Open the transaction for an atomic=True action. Run the handler , then check its value against the return annotation (a mismatch is 500 internal_error , inside the transaction, unless the action sets validate_response=False ) and render it. A returned Response is neither checked nor rendered. Commit after the response is prepared. An exception or cancellation rolls back before the HTTP error is produced. An unhandled exception never becomes a successful response, and a failed commit is an error. A renderer must not perform hidden database I/O.

docs.text: Setting Default When exceeded execution.request_timeout 30 s, through response preparation 504 timeout ; an open transaction rolls back execution.max_body_bytes 1 MiB (also each multipart part) 413 payload_too_large execution.max_query_bytes 8 KiB 414 uri_too_long execution.max_header_bytes 32 KiB, names and values combined 431 headers_too_large execution.max_streams 64 open streams per worker 503 with Retry-After: 1 , before the handler runs The size checks run before routing. A sync handler already running when the timeout expires cannot be stopped: it keeps its executor slot until it returns, and its result is discarded. Let the proxy or ASGI server enforce its own request-line and header limits too.

docs.text: Register routes ¶ An application serves the route map that [project] routes in hinoki.toml points to. Registering an app in hinoki.toml and exposing its HTTP routes in the project's routes.py are two separate decisions. From the manifest to the application ¶ # hinoki.toml [project] application = "notes.main:app" routes = "notes.routes:routes" # the project's single route map [[apps]] name = "billing" models = "notes.apps.billing.models" migrations = "notes.apps.billing.migrations" requires = [] # notes/routes.py from hinoki import Includable , Mount from notes.api import health from notes.apps.billing.routes import routes as billing_routes routes : list [ Includable ] = [ health , Mount ( "/billing" , billing_routes ), ] # notes/main.py from hinoki import Hinoki from notes.settings import ProjectSettings app = Hinoki ( settings = ProjectSettings , title = "Notes" , openapi_url = "/openapi.json" , docs_url = "/docs" , ) # routes, rules, events and middleware come from hinoki.toml When the module named by project.application builds Hinoki(...) without include= , it loads [project] routes automatically ( [] if omitted). Passing include= explicitly (even include=[] ) always wins over the manifest, which is useful for tests or conditional routes. manifest_routes() reads [project] routes explicitly for scripts or separate modules, and raises ProjectError outside a project. hinoki app create billing scaffolds notes/apps/billing/routes.py and prints the Mount("/billing", billing_routes) snippet to add to notes/routes.py if you want to expose the app over HTTP. An app registered in hinoki.toml without a Mount(...) in notes/routes.py still participates in migrations, events and requires without serving HTTP endpoints; an API-only app created with hinoki app create gateway --no-models (or hinoki app add gateway ) has no models or migrations and is mounted in notes/routes.py like any other app. One place for each prefix ¶ Segment Declared by Example The app Mount(...) in the project's routes.py /billing A version inside the app Mount in the app's routes.py /v2 The resource RouteGroup(...) or API, path=... /invoices Write each segment once. Paths inside an app stay relative to the app, so the same app package can be mounted at different prefixes in different projects. Versions with Mount ¶ Mount(prefix, *items) prepends its prefix to everything it holds. Use it inside routes.py when one app serves several versions: # notes/apps/billing/routes.py from hinoki import Includable , Mount from . import v1 , v2 routes : list [ Includable ] = [ Mount ( "/v1" , v1 . routes ), Mount ( "/v2" , v2 . routes ), ] The result is /billing/v1/invoices and /billing/v2/invoices . Mounts nest, and their prefixes join from the outside in. A prefix starts with / and does not end with one, and a mount holds at least one item. Mounting changes the path only: access, errors and transactions stay as declared. What include accepts ¶ Includable is the type of every item a routes list may hold: Item Example A decorated function health A RouteGroup invoices An API class, including a @crud class Invoices A crud(...) value crud(Invoice, path="/invoices", read=InvoiceOut) A Mount Mount("/v1", v1.routes) An object with an api() method the admin A list or tuple of these v1.routes Nested lists are spread in place, in the order you wrote them. Annotate each list as routes: list[Includable] so the type checker rejects anything else; a module passed instead of its list is refused with a hint to export a list. The application module ¶ Declare app once, at module level, in the module that project.application names. Importing it reads the settings and builds declarations; nothing connects until a worker starts, so commands, servers and tests import the same object. A factory target ( module:create_app ) is still accepted by the commands, for code that must build the application from runtime values. Routes for tests and options ¶ To serve a subset, or the same routes with other settings, build another Hinoki with an explicit include= : # tests/billingroutestest.py from hinoki import Hinoki , Mount from notes.apps.billing.routes import routes app = Hinoki ( include = [ Mount ( "/billing" , routes )]) include=[] is an empty application. To add routes that exist only when a setting is on, call app.include(...) in the application module before it serves: # notes/main.py (continued) from hinoki import Mount from notes.apps.billing.exports import exports if app . settings . billing_exports : app . include ( Mount ( "/billing" , exports )) Inspect the map ¶ hinoki routes hinoki routes --path /billing --method POST hinoki routes --format json Rows are sorted by path, then method, and show the effective access policy and the handler. --lanes adds the serving lane of each route. See list routes with routes for every option. Errors and edge cases ¶ Everything below fails when the application is built, before it serves a request: Message Cause cannot load the routes of app 'billing' (notes.apps.billing.routes:routes): … The module or attribute in hinoki.toml does not import the routes of app 'billing' (…) must be a list of routes routes is a single item, not a list or tuple RegistrationError naming an action Two routes reach the same method and path after prefixes join RegistrationError: application is already serving; it is frozen app.include(...) after the server started An include call registers all its items or none of them.
