docs.text: WebSockets ¶ @http.websocket declares a WebSocket action the way @http.get declares an HTTP one. The handler is an async def that receives an http.WebSocket and exchanges whole messages with the client: text, binary or JSON checked against a Schema . # chat/echo.py from hinoki import http from chat.security import member # an `Access` policy @http . websocket ( "/echo" , access = member ) async def echo ( socket : http . WebSocket ) -> None : async for text in socket : await socket . send_text ( text ) Include it like any other action ( Hinoki(include=[echo]) , routes.py , Mount ). The connection ends when the handler returns (close code 1000 ), when the client closes, or when the handler raises ( 1011 ). What runs where ¶ On Kiso, the WebSocket protocol runs in Rust: the handshake, frame parsing and masking, text validation, fragmentation, ping and pong, the close handshake, the size limits and the timers. The handler only sees whole messages through two bounded queues; Python runs the handler and, at the handshake, access and the argument binding. Messages cross the Python boundary as str and bytes . WebSocket over HTTP/2, permessage-deflate and other extensions are not provided; a client that offers extensions gets none. Under Granian (any ASGI server) the same actions run through the ASGI websocket scope. The server owns the frames, so Hinoki enforces only what a Python layer can: the Origin check, the message size and the handler lifecycle. The ping interval, idle timeout, max_websockets and the queue size do not apply; use the server's own options. The handshake ¶ The handshake is an HTTP GET , so the usual answers apply before the connection is upgraded and the handler never starts for a refused client: Answer When 426 the request is not a WebSocket upgrade, or asks for a version other than 13 (the answer names Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13 ) 400 an invalid Sec-WebSocket-Key , an unsupported subprotocol, or a path or query value that is not valid 401 , 403 access refused the caller 403 the Origin is not allowed 503 execution.max_websockets connections are open A WebSocket path may not also be an HTTP GET route with the same pattern. On Kiso a plain GET that a more specific HTTP route matches ( /rooms/stats beside /rooms/{room} ) goes to the HTTP route; only upgrade requests reach the WebSocket action. A path with a parameter is declared as in HTTP: @http.websocket("/rooms/{room}") . Path and query values are bound to handler parameters typed str , int , float , bool or UUID ; a parameter with a default is optional. A malformed value is refused with 400 before the upgrade. Annotations are read when the action is included, so a handler may name a type defined later in its module; an unsupported parameter type is a RegistrationError at Hinoki(include=...) . The decorator keeps the handler's signature for type checkers. Under ASGI, Hinoki waits for the server's websocket.connect event before it answers: a refusal is sent only to a client that connected, and a client gone before connecting gets nothing. On an API class ¶ An API class may declare WebSocket actions next to its HTTP ones. The path is joined to the class prefix, and the handler gets a fresh instance as self for each connection, so the class must be constructible without arguments. @http.websocket on a staticmethod or classmethod is refused. from hinoki import API , http class Rooms ( API , path = "/rooms" ): @http . websocket ( "/ {room} " ) async def join ( self , room : str , socket : http . WebSocket ) -> None : await socket . send_text ( f "welcome to { room } " ) Access and the caller ¶ access= takes the same reusable Access as an HTTP action and is judged on the handshake request: its headers, cookies and query string. A browser cannot set an Authorization header on a WebSocket, so use a cookie or a provider that reads the query. A parameter annotated Caller receives the authenticated caller, as in HTTP. Authorization of what each message may do stays in your handler, which is also where tenant or ownership checks belong; WebSocket actions are not part of generated CRUD. # chat/security.py from hinoki import Access , BearerAuth , Caller class Tokens ( BearerAuth [ str ]): async def resolve_token ( self , token : str ) -> Caller [ str ] | None : ... # look the token up; return None when it is unknown READ = Access ( Tokens (), permissions = [ "chat:read" ]) # chat/inbox.py from hinoki import Caller , http from chat.security import READ @http . websocket ( "/inbox" , access = READ ) async def inbox ( who : Caller [ str ], socket : http . WebSocket ) -> None : await socket . send_text ( f "hello { who . id } " ) Origin ¶ A request without an Origin header (not a browser) is accepted. A request with one must match the host the request was sent to, an origin listed in origins= on the route ( origins=["https://app.example"] , or "*" ), or an origin the application's CORS policy lists by name. A CORS wildcard ( cors origins * ) is not honoured here: a browser sends cookies on a WebSocket handshake and does not hide the answer from other sites, so an open policy would let any site use a cookie-authenticated action. Anything else is refused with 403 before the upgrade. On Granian the check covers the same sources, through the same Rust predicate. The same-host match requires the scheme the connection has: https:// where the connection is https (direct TLS, a trusted proxy reporting https , or wss on Granian) and http:// otherwise, never both. Behind a proxy that terminates TLS without reporting the scheme, list the page's origin in origins= or the CORS origins. The host is compared exactly, in lower case, port included: no default port or trailing dot is folded in. Granian handshakes also go through allowed_hosts and trusted-proxy handling, and the route is matched on the raw path, as for HTTP requests. The same-host match trusts the Host header, so an app with WebSocket routes and allowed_hosts left at * refuses to start unless debug is on, which is for local development only; with debug on the app then accepts loopback Host names only ( localhost , *.localhost , 127.0.0.0/8 , [::1] ), any other Host receives 400 , and a handshake to it is refused. Name the served hosts with allowed_hosts to serve other names. Subprotocols ¶ subprotocols= names the subprotocols an action speaks, each an HTTP token (letters, digits and !#$%&'*+-.^_`|~ , so chat.v1 but not chat/v1 ). The server picks the first one the client offered and returns it in the 101 answer ( socket.subprotocol ). A client that offers none of them is refused with 400 . A mapping gives each subprotocol its own Access , which runs after the action's: # chat/feed.py from hinoki import http from chat.security import READ @http . websocket ( "/feed" , subprotocols = { "public.v1" : None , "staff.v1" : READ }) async def feed ( socket : http . WebSocket ) -> None : await socket . send_text ( socket . subprotocol or "" ) Messages ¶ Call Result await socket.receive_text() the next text message; a binary one closes with 1003 await socket.receive_bytes() the next binary message; a text one closes with 1003 await socket.receive_json(schema=None) text parsed as JSON, then validated against the Schema given or the route's message await socket.send_text(text) , send_bytes(data) queue a message, waiting while the outgoing queue is full await socket.send_json(value) a JSON text message; with reply= on the route, a dict is validated against it and an instance of a subclass of it is sent with the fields of reply only await socket.close(code=1000, reason="") close after the queued messages async for message in socket each message, until the connection ends; with message= on the route, each is a validated Schema instance Reading or sending on a closed connection raises http.WebSocketClosed (with code and reason ); a handler may let it propagate, since it is not an error. Text that is not JSON closes with 1007 , JSON that fails validation with 1008 . from hinoki import Schema , http from chat.security import READ class Move ( Schema ): x : int y : int class Position ( Schema ): x : int y : int by : str @http . websocket ( "/board" , access = READ , message = Move , reply = Position ) async def board ( socket : http . WebSocket ) -> None : async for move in socket : await socket . send_json ({ "x" : move . x + 1 , "y" : move . y , "by" : "server" }) Limits and back-pressure ¶ Settings under execution (see settings ); each is enforced by Kiso: Setting Default Effect max_websockets 1000 open connections per worker; more are refused with 503 before the upgrade ws_max_message_bytes 1048576 a message (reassembled from its frames) over this closes with 1009 ; max_message_bytes= on the route overrides it ws_queue 64 messages queued in each direction; a slow handler stops being read from, so TCP back-pressure reaches the client, and send_* waits while the client is slow ws_ping_interval 20.0 seconds between pings; None turns them off ws_pong_timeout 20.0 a peer that does not answer a ping within this is dropped (reported to the handler as 1006 ) ws_close_timeout 5.0 how long the close handshake may take before the connection is dropped idle_timeout= on the route (seconds without a data message from the client, closing with 1001 ) is off by default, since a server-push connection can be silent from the client on purpose. Frames that are malformed, unmasked from a client, reserved or oversized control frames, invalid UTF-8 in text, and bad close codes end the connection with 1002 or 1007 as RFC 6455 requires. A fragmented message may span at most 4,096 frames, its first one included; a fragment past that ends the connection with 1002 , whatever the message size. A write that makes no progress for execution.request_timeout seconds drops the connection. Shutdown and reload ¶ When the server stops, Kiso closes every open connection with 1001 and the handler's receive and send calls end ( async for stops, the explicit calls raise http.WebSocketClosed ). Connections are part of the graceful drain, so they get the shutdown timeout to finish and are aborted after it. A SIGHUP reload replaces a worker through the same graceful stop, so its connections get 1001 and a client is expected to reconnect, which reaches the new worker. OpenAPI ¶ OpenAPI 3.1 and 3.2 have no WebSocket operation, so the document describes the actions under the vendor extension x-hinoki-websockets , keyed by path: the handler docstring, the message and reply schema components, the subprotocols, the origins and the handshake's security requirement. They are not listed under paths . Not provided ¶ WebSocket over HTTP/2, permessage-deflate , @http.websocket on a RouteGroup , and a native (GIL-free) handler lane for WebSockets.

docs.text: Settings under execution (see settings ); each is enforced by Kiso: Setting Default Effect max_websockets 1000 open connections per worker; more are refused with 503 before the upgrade ws_max_message_bytes 1048576 a message (reassembled from its frames) over this closes with 1009 ; max_message_bytes= on the route overrides it ws_queue 64 messages queued in each direction; a slow handler stops being read from, so TCP back-pressure reaches the client, and send_* waits while the client is slow ws_ping_interval 20.0 seconds between pings; None turns them off ws_pong_timeout 20.0 a peer that does not answer a ping within this is dropped (reported to the handler as 1006 ) ws_close_timeout 5.0 how long the close handshake may take before the connection is dropped idle_timeout= on the route (seconds without a data message from the client, closing with 1001 ) is off by default, since a server-push connection can be silent from the client on purpose. Frames that are malformed, unmasked from a client, reserved or oversized control frames, invalid UTF-8 in text, and bad close codes end the connection with 1002 or 1007 as RFC 6455 requires. A fragmented message may span at most 4,096 frames, its first one included; a fragment past that ends the connection with 1002 , whatever the message size. A write that makes no progress for execution.request_timeout seconds drops the connection.
docs.title: Limits and back-pressure

docs.text: When the server stops, Kiso closes every open connection with 1001 and the handler's receive and send calls end ( async for stops, the explicit calls raise http.WebSocketClosed ). Connections are part of the graceful drain, so they get the shutdown timeout to finish and are aborted after it. A SIGHUP reload replaces a worker through the same graceful stop, so its connections get 1001 and a client is expected to reconnect, which reaches the new worker.
docs.title: Shutdown and reload

They are not listed under paths .

docs.text: Auth and crypto ¶ JWTAuth delegates signature and registered-claim verification to the Rust core. Its current key and policy values are captured for each token verification, while the application-defined resolve_claims hook remains Python and runs for every verified token. hinoki.auth.Caller dataclass ¶ Caller ( id : str , user : T , permissions : Iterable [ str ] = (), claims : Mapping [ str , Any ] = _EMPTY_CLAIMS , ) Who is making the request, as decided by authentication. id is a stable string, user is your own object (the user row, a service account) and permissions is what the caller may do:: Caller(id="u1", user=user, permissions=frozenset({"posts:write"})) hinoki.auth.Permission ¶ Bases: StrEnum Base for an application's typed permission names. Subclass it with the permissions your application uses:: class BlogPermission(Permission): WRITE = "posts:write" Members compare and serialize as their string values. hinoki.auth.Credentials dataclass ¶ Credentials ( headers : Mapping [ str , str ], query : dict [ str , list [ str ]], session : object | None = None , ) The parts of a request a provider may inspect. hinoki.auth.BaseAuth ¶ Bases: ABC Base class of providers. authenticate returns a principal, None when the request carries no credentials, and raises Unauthorized when credentials are present but invalid. Providers hold no per-request state. uses_session class-attribute instance-attribute ¶ uses_session : bool = False True for a provider that reads Credentials.session . The request is then given its application session before authentication, and unsafe methods carrying a session cookie must pass the session CSRF check. A provider that holds others (as attributes, or in a list or tuple) uses the session when any of them does. openapi_scheme ¶ openapi_scheme () -> dict [ str , object ] | None OpenAPI security scheme describing this provider, if it has one. authenticate abstractmethod ¶ authenticate ( credentials : Credentials , ) -> Caller [ T ] | Awaitable [ Caller [ T ] | None ] | None async def or plain def (a plain one runs on the sync executor). hinoki.auth.HeaderAuth ¶ Bases: BaseAuth [ T ] Credential carried in a named header; subclasses implement resolve . resolve abstractmethod ¶ resolve ( value : str , ) -> Caller [ T ] | Awaitable [ Caller [ T ] | None ] | None The principal for a header value or None if invalid; async def or plain def . hinoki.auth.BearerAuth ¶ Bases: HeaderAuth [ T ] Authorization: Bearer <token> ; subclasses implement resolve_token . resolve_token abstractmethod ¶ resolve_token ( token : str , ) -> Caller [ T ] | Awaitable [ Caller [ T ] | None ] | None async def or plain def , as resolve . hinoki.auth.APIKeyAuth ¶ Bases: HeaderAuth [ T ] API key in x-api-key (override header to change it). hinoki.crypto.JWTKey dataclass ¶ JWTKey ( kid : str | None , algorithm : str , key : bytes | str | Secret , public : bool = False , ) One verification (and optionally signing) key. HMAC secrets must be at least as long as the hash (32/48/64 bytes). For EdDSA the key is the 32-byte private seed, or with public=True the 32-byte public key of a verify-only deployment. key is bytes, text or a Secret (such as a Settings field). kid is required when several keys are configured. The key is excluded from repr . verify_only classmethod ¶ verify_only ( kid : str | None , public_key : bytes ) -> JWTKey An Ed25519 public key (32 bytes) that can verify but never sign. Use this, not the plain constructor, wherever you hold only the public key: a public key passed as a seed would let anyone who knows it forge tokens. hinoki.crypto.JWTAuth ¶ JWTAuth () Bases: BearerAuth [ T ] Bearer-token provider for JWTs. Subclass, set keys (and usually issuer and audience ) and implement resolve_claims :: class Tokens(JWTAuth[User]): keys = [JWTKey("2026-11", "HS256", settings.jwt_secret)] issuer = "https://api.example.com" audience = "blog" async def resolve_claims(self, claims): subject, raw = claims.get("sub"), claims.get("scopes", []) if not isinstance(subject, str) or not isinstance(raw, list): return None # claims are signed, but still untyped JSON try: user = await User.aget_or_none(id=UUID(subject)) except ValueError: # a signed token can still carry any text return None if user is None: return None scopes = frozenset(s for s in raw if isinstance(s, str)) return Caller(subject, user, scopes) now ¶ now () -> int The clock (override in tests). resolve_claims abstractmethod ¶ resolve_claims ( claims : dict [ str , Any ], ) -> Caller [ T ] | Awaitable [ Caller [ T ] | None ] | None The principal for verified claims, or None to refuse; async def or plain def . issue ¶ issue ( claims : dict [ str , Any ], ttl : int = 900 ) -> str A signed token for claims valid for ttl seconds, signed with the first non-public key. iat and exp are always set by the server (a value in claims is replaced); iss and aud are added when configured, unless claims already has them. hinoki.crypto.ClaimsJWTAuth ¶ ClaimsJWTAuth () Bases: JWTAuth [None] A JWT provider whose caller comes from the signed claims alone. Subclass it and set keys (and usually issuer and audience ):: class Tokens(ClaimsJWTAuth): keys = [JWTKey("2026-11", "HS256", settings.jwt_secret)] Caller.id is the non-empty string claim sub , Caller.user is None and Caller.permissions are the strings in the list claim named by scope_claim (none when it is absent). A token without a usable sub , or whose scope claim is not a list, is refused. Nothing is loaded from a database, so a token stays valid until it expires; use JWTAuth when a revoked or deleted account must be refused immediately. Because it runs no application code, the Rust server can authenticate generated CRUD routes that use it without entering Python. Overriding any method keeps the routes on the Python request pipeline. hinoki.crypto.PasswordHasher ¶ PasswordHasher ( * , memory_kib : int = MIN_MEMORY_KIB , time_cost : int = MIN_TIME_COST , lanes : int = 1 , workers : int = 2 , max_pending : int = 64 , allow_weak : bool = False , ) Argon2id hashes in PHC format, computed off the event loop. Parameters below the OWASP floor are refused unless allow_weak=True (tests only). workers bounds concurrent hashing, max_pending the queue; beyond that hash / verify raise HashingBusy (503). A task cancelled while its hash runs frees its slot but the thread finishes, so at most workers extra hashes can be in flight; hash_sync / verify_sync are not bounded. Only argon2id hashes are verified. For unknown users, verify against a fixed dummy hash so timing does not reveal who exists. The thread pool starts with the first hash / verify and stops with close() (or at the end of a with / async with block); a closed hasher starts a new pool when it is used again. A hasher that is never closed stops its pool when it is garbage-collected. pool property ¶ pool : ThreadPoolExecutor The hashing threads, started on first use. hash_sync ¶ hash_sync ( password : str ) -> str Blocking hash (for scripts and sync handlers). verify_sync ¶ verify_sync ( password : str , stored : str ) -> bool False for a wrong password; ValueError for a malformed hash. needs_rehash ¶ needs_rehash ( stored : str ) -> bool True when stored was made with other parameters than these. close ¶ close () -> None Stop the hashing threads; queued work is cancelled. Idempotent. hinoki.crypto.random_token ¶ random_token ( size : int = 32 ) -> str size random bytes (1 to 1024) as URL-safe text, from the OS CSPRNG.

docs.text: Parsers and renderers ¶ hinoki.parsers.Parser ¶ Base class of body parsers. hinoki.parsers.JSONParser ¶ Bases: Parser JSON, decoded by the Rust parser (strict: no NaN, no lone surrogates, depth limit). Customise by overriding prepare(data) to reshape the decoded value (for example rename keys) or media_type ( application/vnd.api+json ). prepare ¶ prepare ( data : object ) -> object Hook: the value the action sees (default: as decoded). hinoki.parsers.FormParser ¶ FormParser ( max_fields : int = DEFAULT_FIELDS ) Bases: Parser application/x-www-form-urlencoded . data holds the last value of each field as text. hinoki.parsers.MultiPartParser ¶ MultiPartParser ( max_parts : int = DEFAULT_PARTS , max_part_bytes : int = DEFAULT_PART_BYTES , ) Bases: Parser multipart/form-data with at most max_parts parts of at most max_part_bytes bytes each (the whole body is capped separately). Selected automatically, with the default limits, for an action that binds an UploadedFile without choosing its parsers; pass it explicitly to change the limits. hinoki.parsers.TextParser ¶ Bases: Parser text/plain bodies as a str (UTF-8, strict). hinoki.parsers.BytesParser ¶ Bases: Parser application/octet-stream bodies as the raw bytes , unchanged. hinoki.parsers.XMLParser ¶ XMLParser ( max_depth : int = DEFAULT_XML_DEPTH , max_elements : int = DEFAULT_XML_ELEMENTS , ) Bases: Parser application/xml . data is the tree under the root element: an element with children is a dict , a repeated child name a list , a text-only element a str and an empty one None . Attributes are not read. DTDs, custom entities, characters XML 1.0 forbids and an encoding other than UTF-8 are refused, and nesting (at most MAX_XML_DEPTH ) and element count are capped. hinoki.parsers.Parsed dataclass ¶ Parsed ( data : object , fields : Mapping [ str , list [ str ]] = dict (), files : Mapping [ str , list [ UploadedFile ]] = dict (), ) What a parser produced: data for request.data plus form fields and files for request.POST / request.FILES . hinoki.errors.InvalidBody ¶ InvalidBody ( code : str , message : str ) Bases: Exception The request body cannot be used at all (wrong media type, bad JSON). hinoki.UploadedFile dataclass ¶ UploadedFile ( name : str , filename : str , content_type : str , content : bytes , ) A multipart file. filename is exactly what the client sent: never use it as a path. hinoki.renderers.Renderer ¶ Base class of response renderers. hinoki.renderers.JSONRenderer ¶ JSONRenderer ( indent : int | None = None , sort_keys : bool = False , default : Callable [[ Any ], Any ] | None = None , ) Bases: Renderer JSON, written by the Rust encoder. Customise without leaving Rust: options: JSONRenderer(indent=2, sort_keys=True, default=fn) where default turns a value that is not JSON (a Decimal , a Path ) into one that is; a subclass overriding prepare(value, request) to reshape the result (envelopes, key renaming) before it is encoded, and/or media_type (for application/vnd.api+json ). prepare ¶ prepare ( value : object , request : Request ) -> object Hook: the value to encode (default: unchanged). hinoki.renderers.HTMLRenderer ¶ Bases: Renderer A handler that returns str answers HTML (UTF-8). The string is sent as is: escape untrusted data before putting it in. hinoki.renderers.TextRenderer ¶ Bases: Renderer A handler that returns str answers plain text (UTF-8). hinoki.renderers.XMLRenderer ¶ XMLRenderer ( root : str = 'response' , item : str = 'item' ) Bases: Renderer The result as XML (UTF-8, with an XML declaration), written by the Rust encoder, which accepts what the JSON encoder accepts. A mapping becomes child elements named by its keys, a list becomes repeated item elements, None an empty element, and true / false are written in lower case. Keys are spelled as JSON spells them ( None as null , booleans true / false , integers in decimal) and any other key is refused, as JSON refuses it. A key that is not a valid XML name (it has a space, starts with a digit, begins with xml ) is written as <item key="..."> instead of failing. Characters XML 1.0 cannot carry are replaced by U+FFFD. XMLRenderer(root="orders", item="order") renames the root element and the list item.

A single Access protects every action; CrudAccess sets them apart. name= names the generated class ( "ArchiveCrud" ) or its module and class ( "notes.apps.archive.ArchiveCrud" ) that rules and MCP patterns match. cors=http.Cors(...) gives every generated action that CORS policy instead of the application's. filters= takes a FilterSet subclass: the list then accepts the filters, ordering and search it declares. omit= drops any generated action ( "list" , "retrieve" , "create" , "update" , "delete" ) so it can be omitted or handwritten instead. include_in_schema=False leaves every generated action out of the OpenAPI document; include_in_schema={"delete": False} leaves out only the named actions. tags and deprecated apply to every action. docs.text: Database API ¶ For setup, application settings, URL examples and migration workflow, see configure a database . The ORM supports PostgreSQL, SQLite, MySQL and MariaDB. SQLite is the local-development default; configure an explicit URL to select a server backend. Raw SQL uses the selected driver's placeholders: PostgreSQL uses $1 , while SQLite, MySQL and MariaDB use ? . ORM-generated queries select the dialect automatically. Configure a backend ¶ Database URLs are secrets, so configure them through the environment rather than TOML. For local development, leave the URL unset to use the default SQLite file. The migration commands read the application's database setting too; HINOKI_DATABASE_URL overrides it for them ( which database ). TOML may configure non-secret pool options, for example: [database] max_size = 8 For PostgreSQL, use a driver URL such as postgresql://user:password@host/db . For MySQL, use mysql://user:password@host/db . MySQL connections require TLS by default; the driver verifies the server certificate and hostname. Configure the system trust store to trust your server certificate. require_ssl=false is only suitable for isolated local testing and disables transport encryption. Do not put production credentials in source-controlled settings files. For MariaDB, use mariadb://user:password@host/db ; it is selected and tested as a distinct backend even though it uses the MySQL wire driver and SQL dialect. Backend behavior and limits ¶ Backend Status Notes SQLite Supported Default for local development. SQLite permits one writer at a time. Table changes that SQLite cannot express directly use a table rebuild. PostgreSQL Supported Uses PostgreSQL-native UUID, timestamp, JSON and byte types. MySQL Supported Uses InnoDB tables, binary UUIDs and MySQL-native JSON. MySQL DDL implicitly commits, so a failed migration can leave earlier DDL applied; inspect migration status and table state before retrying. RETURNING is not supported by the compiler; ORM create/update operations use follow-up reads. TLS is required by default. MariaDB Supported Tested independently on MariaDB 11.4. Its JSON alias is text, so typed ORM dict / list fields are decoded from the model declaration. Low-level Database.fetch() returns JSON values as bytes because arbitrary text columns cannot be safely inferred as JSON. DDL can implicitly commit; TLS is required by default. SQL Server and Oracle are not currently supported. Do not assume that MySQL compatibility implies MariaDB compatibility. Hinoki does not silently roll back MySQL-family DDL: review generated migrations and keep a recoverable backup before applying migrations. Datetime values stored in MySQL DATETIME columns use Hinoki's UTC-naive storage convention; values returned by the ORM are interpreted as UTC. MySQL pool capacity and acquisition wait are bounded by the database pool settings. Raw SQL must use the placeholders for the configured backend. Prefer ORM query methods when the same code should work across backends; raw SQL and migration operations may need backend-specific SQL. hinoki.db.Database ¶ Database ( engine : Database ) Bases: Resource A connection pool for one configured database backend. engine instance-attribute ¶ engine = engine dialect property ¶ dialect : str The selected dialect: postgres , sqlite , mysql or mariadb . connect async classmethod ¶ connect ( url : str , * , max_size : int = 10 , wait : float = 5.0 ) -> Database Open the pool and check the server; PostgreSQL URLs may configure TLS. active ¶ active () -> ActiveTransaction | None fetch async ¶ fetch ( sql : str , * params : Param ) -> list [ Row ] Rows as dicts, with placeholders selected by the active backend. fetch_models async ¶ fetch_models ( sql : str , params : list [ Any ], plan : _ModelRows ) -> list [ Any ] Rows built into finished model instances (private; QuerySet.fetch ). fetch_page_models async ¶ fetch_page_models ( rows_sql : str , rows_params : list [ Any ], count_sql : str , count_params : list [ Any ], plan : _ModelRows , * , concurrent : bool = False , ) -> tuple [ list [ Any ], int ] Fetch one page of model instances and its total count (private). fetch_page_rows async ¶ fetch_page_rows ( rows_sql : str , rows_params : list [ Any ], count_sql : str , count_params : list [ Any ], * , concurrent : bool = False , ) -> tuple [ list [ Row ], int ] Fetch one page of raw rows and its total count (private). fetch_projected_list async ¶ fetch_projected_list ( sql : str , params : list [ Any ], plan : _RowPlan ) -> _ProjectedRows | list [ Row ] Fetch rows pre-encoded to JSON by Rust, or raw rows on fallback. fetch_projected_one async ¶ fetch_projected_one ( sql : str , params : list [ Any ], plan : _RowPlan ) -> _ProjectedRows | list [ Row ] | str | None Fetch one row pre-encoded to JSON by Rust, None if empty, "multiple" if >1 row, or raw rows on fallback. fetch_projected_page async ¶ fetch_projected_page ( rows_sql : str , rows_params : list [ Any ], count_sql : str , count_params : list [ Any ], plan : _RowPlan , page_window : tuple [ int , int ], * , concurrent : bool = False , ) -> _ProjectedRows | tuple [ list [ Row ], int ] Fetch one page pre-encoded to JSON by Rust, or raw rows on fallback. fetch_one async ¶ fetch_one ( sql : str , * params : Param ) -> Row | None execute async ¶ execute ( sql : str , * params : Param ) -> int Number of affected rows; raw SQL placeholders follow the backend. atomic ¶ atomic () -> AtomicScope async with database.atomic(): — commit on success, roll back on any exception; inside an open scope of the same task, a savepoint. after_commit ¶ after_commit ( callback : Callable [[], object ]) -> None Run callback (sync or async) after the outermost transaction commits, in registration order. A rollback, of the transaction or of the savepoint scope it was registered in, drops it; an exception in a callback is logged and does not undo the commit. migration ¶ migration () -> AtomicScope An exclusive migration transaction with backend locking semantics. close ¶ close () -> None status ¶ status () -> tuple [ int , int ] (connections, idle) in the pool. hinoki.db.atomic ¶ atomic ( func : Callable [ P , Coroutine [ Any , Any , R ]], ) -> Callable [ P , Coroutine [ Any , Any , R ]] atomic ( func : Callable [ P , R ]) -> Callable [ P , R ] atomic () -> Atomic atomic ( func : Callable [ ... , Any ] | None = None ) -> Any async with db.atomic(): , with db.atomic(): , @db.atomic or @db.atomic() : run a block or a function, async def or plain def , atomically on the current database. The sync forms are for sync handlers. hinoki.db.Atomic ¶ db.atomic() : an atomic scope on the current database, as a block or as a decorator. async with db.atomic(): opens current_database().atomic() when the block is entered; with db.atomic(): does the same in a sync handler. Decorating an async def or a plain def opens a fresh scope for every call: returning commits, an exception rolls back, and a call made inside an already atomic scope becomes a savepoint. leave ¶ leave () -> AtomicScope Pop this task's innermost open scope. hinoki.db.AtomicScope ¶ AtomicScope ( database : Database , * , migration : bool = False ) async with database.atomic(): — commit, rollback or savepoint. open async ¶ open ( * , shared : bool ) -> None Begin the transaction, or a savepoint inside the open one. shared lets a scope opened by a different task of a sync handler's thread nest. leave_savepoint async ¶ leave_savepoint ( state : ActiveTransaction , ok : bool ) -> None Release the savepoint, or roll back to it and then release it: a ROLLBACK TO keeps the savepoint open. content_type is type/subtype . hinoki.mail.SentMail dataclass ¶ SentMail ( message_id : str , recipients : tuple [ str , ... ], attempts : int , raw : bytes | None = None , message : Message | None = None , ) What send returns. recipients are the envelope addresses in their normalized form. raw (the rendered message) and message are kept by the console and memory backends only. hinoki.mail.Mailer ¶ Mailer ( settings : EmailSettings , templates : Sequence [ TemplateBase ] = (), ) The email resource of one worker: it owns the connection pool of the smtp backend, so create it inside a running worker ( EmailModule does) and never at import. aclose refuses later sends and closes the idle connections; call it before the loop ends. outbox property ¶ outbox : tuple [ SentMail , ... ] The messages the memory backend kept, oldest first (at most memory_capacity : the oldest are dropped). send async ¶ send ( message : Message ) -> SentMail Deliver message ; raises EmailError . check async ¶ check () -> None smtp : connect, start TLS and authenticate with a new connection, then quit; nothing is sent. The other backends do nothing. aclose async ¶ aclose () -> None Close the mailer; safe to call twice. A later send raises EmailError of kind closed . stats ¶ stats () -> MailerStats clear_outbox ¶ clear_outbox () -> None loaded_template ¶ loaded_template ( template : TemplateBase , ) -> core . MailTemplate The compiled form of a template registered with this mailer (file templates were read when it started). RuntimeError when the template is not one of the ones the mailer was built with. hinoki.mail.EmailModule ¶ EmailModule ( settings : EmailSettings , templates : Sequence [ TemplateBase ] = (), ) Bases: Module Opens a Mailer in each worker's lifespan and provides it ( ctx.get(Mailer) ); installed automatically by an email: EmailSettings field. With check_on_startup the lifespan connects first and a failure aborts the start. mailer property ¶ mailer : Mailer The mailer of the running (most recently started) lifespan; for tests that inspect the outbox of an application they drive. templates property ¶ templates : tuple [ TemplateBase , ... ] The templates this module registers, in the order given. from_settings classmethod ¶ from_settings ( settings : object , templates : Sequence [ TemplateBase ] = () ) -> EmailModule hinoki.mail.EmailError ¶ EmailError ( kind : EmailErrorKind , * , code : int | None = None , enhanced_status : str | None = None , attempts : int = 0 , possibly_sent : bool = False , field : str | None = None , index : int | None = None , ) Bases: Exception A message was refused or could not be delivered. str(error) is a fixed sentence for kind plus the position or reply code: never an address, the subject, the body, the server's text or a credential. code and enhanced_status are the SMTP reply's when one came; attempts the delivery attempts made; field and index where a validation failure is ( index is the position in that tuple); possibly_sent is true only when the end of the message was written and no reply came, so the server may have accepted it (do not blindly resend). hinoki.mail.EmailErrorKind ¶ Bases: StrEnum hinoki.mail.Template ¶ Template ( * , name : str , subject : str , html : str , text : str | None = None , context : type [ S ], description : str | None = None , ) Template ( * , name : str , subject : str , html : str , text : str | None = None , context : None = None , description : str | None = None , ) Template ( * , name : str , subject : str , html : str , text : str | None = None , context : type [ Schema ] | None = None , description : str | None = None , ) Bases: TemplateBase An email template: a subject, an HTML body and optionally a text body, written in the small template language of docs/email-templates.md . context= names the Schema the template is written for: its fields are the variables, and every variable and every field is checked when the template is compiled. A Schema context is dumped by field name ( dump(by_alias=False) ); raises TemplateError , TypeError for a context of the wrong type. message ¶ message ( context : C , * , to : tuple [ Recipient , ... ] = (), ** options : Unpack [ MessageOptions ], ) -> Message A Message of the rendered parts, ready for mail.send . A template that cannot be rendered counts as a failed send of the current mailer (outcome template ) and raises TemplateError . hinoki.mail.TemplateBase ¶ TemplateBase ( * , name : str , description : str | None , context_type : type [ Schema ] | None , origin : MailTemplate | Path , ) What every template is, whatever its context type: the name registries key on, a description, the file it is read from (if any) and the context Schema (if any). path property ¶ path : Path | None The file of a template made with Template.file . loaded property ¶ loaded : bool Whether the template is compiled already: true for an inline template, false for a file one (each worker's mailer reads it at startup). load ¶ load () -> core . MailTemplate The compiled template. A file template is read, parsed, compiled and checked now (synchronously): at most MAX_FILE_BYTES are read. compiled ¶ compiled () -> core . MailTemplate The compiled template: itself when inline, the one the current worker's mailer loaded for a file template. hinoki.mail.TemplateError ¶ TemplateError ( * , template : str , problems : Sequence [ TemplateProblem ], truncated : bool = False , ) Bases: EmailError A template is invalid or cannot be rendered. kind is always EmailErrorKind.TEMPLATE ; problems lists what is wrong (the first is mirrored in reason , field (the part), line , column and variable ) and truncated tells that more were found. str(error) names the template, the reason, the part, the position and the variable; never a context value, a recipient or rendered text. hinoki.mail.TemplateReason ¶ Bases: StrEnum Why a template was refused: the names the engine reports. hinoki.mail.TemplateProblem dataclass ¶ TemplateProblem ( reason : TemplateReason , part : str | None = None , line : int | None = None , column : int | None = None , variable : str | None = None , ) One thing wrong with a template. part is "subject" , "text" or "html" ; line and column (from 1) point into that part of the template source; variable is a name from the template or the Schema , never a value of the context. hinoki.mail.RenderedTemplate dataclass ¶ RenderedTemplate ( subject : str , text : str , html : str ) The three parts of a rendered template. hinoki.mail.Context ¶ Context = Mapping [ str , Value ] The context of a template declared without a Schema . hinoki.mail.Value ¶ Value = ( str | int | float | bool | list [ Value ] | tuple [ Value , ... ] | dict [ str , Value ] | None ) What a template context holds. (or the compatible table= class keyword) to derive the table name <app>_<models> from the model's package and class name; label= and plural= override humanized display names. NotFound class-attribute ¶ NotFound : type [ ObjectNotFound ] = ObjectNotFound is_new property ¶ is_new : bool True until the row has been written or loaded. is_dirty property ¶ is_dirty : bool True for a new instance and for one whose columns differ from the stored values. changes property ¶ changes : dict [ str , Change ] The columns that differ from the stored row, as Change(old, new) . A new instance reports every column with old=UNSET . Computed when read: nothing is tracked on assignment. changed_fields property ¶ changed_fields : tuple [ str , ... ] Names of columns that differ from the stored snapshot. is_deleted property ¶ is_deleted : bool Whether this row has a soft-delete timestamp. check_field_conflicts classmethod ¶ check_field_conflicts () -> None Two bases may not give one field name different types: which one the model would get depends on base order, and the other would be lost. A base that overrides its own parent, or the class redeclaring the field, is a decision and is accepted. check_field_validations classmethod ¶ check_field_validations ( columns : tuple [ Field [ Any ], ... ], annotations : dict [ str , object ], ) -> dict [ str , FieldType ] Validate constraints against annotations, refuse a column type no migration can create and reject async callbacks. validate_values classmethod ¶ validate_values ( values : dict [ str , Any ]) -> dict [ str , Any ] Run declared field checks on values about to be written and return them as they are stored: strip , lower and upper applied. adopt_mixin_fields classmethod ¶ adopt_mixin_fields () -> None Field annotations of plain (non-model, non-dataclass) bases become fields of this class. dataclasses reads only a class's own annotations and its dataclass bases, so without this a mixin's fields would be dropped without a word. option_bases classmethod ¶ option_bases () -> list [ type [ Model ]] The abstract models this class is declared on. A decorator applied to this class later replaces what was inherited for its kind (see hinoki.orm.options ). docs.text: Concrete models may omit @db.table(...) (or the compatible table= class keyword) to derive the table name <app>_<models> from the model's package and class name; label= and plural= override humanized display names. Explicit table names remain the safe choice for migration-backed histories and stable physical names.

Indexes declared with field(index=True) belong to their column: they stay while the column keeps index=True and go when this class redeclares the column without it, whether or not a decorator is applied.

A synchronous or asynchronous handle is supported. name class-attribute ¶ name : str = '' help class-attribute ¶ help : str = '' requires class-attribute ¶ requires : tuple [ type [ Module ], ... ] = () add_arguments ¶ add_arguments ( parser : ArgumentParser ) -> None Add command-specific arguments to the parser. handle ¶ handle ( context : CommandContext , args : Namespace ) -> CommandResult Run the command; return an optional process exit code. hinoki.management.CommandContext ¶ CommandContext ( settings : object | None , modules : ModuleContext ) Settings and resources available during one command invocation. settings instance-attribute ¶ settings = settings get ¶ get ( kind : type [ T ]) -> T Return a module resource or raise LookupError if unavailable. find ¶ find ( kind : type [ T ]) -> T | None Return a module resource, or None when it is unavailable. hinoki.management.CommandError ¶ Bases: Exception The command could not start or returned an invalid result. hinoki.runtime.config.RuntimeConfig dataclass ¶ RuntimeConfig ( sync_workers : int = 8 , sync_queue : int = 64 , request_timeout : float = 30.0 , startup_timeout : float = 30.0 , shutdown_timeout : float = 10.0 , max_body_bytes : int = 1024 * 1024 , max_query_bytes : int = 8192 , max_header_bytes : int = 32768 , max_streams : int = 64 , stream_idle_timeout : float | None = None , sse_keepalive : float = 15.0 , max_websockets : int = 1000 , ws_max_message_bytes : int = 1024 * 1024 , ws_queue : int = 64 , ws_ping_interval : float | None = 20.0 , ws_pong_timeout : float = 20.0 , ws_close_timeout : float = 5.0 , ) idle_timeout property ¶ idle_timeout : float Seconds a stream's producer may stay silent. hinoki.errors.ModuleGraphError ¶ Bases: RegistrationError Missing dependency, dependency cycle or duplicate module name. hinoki.errors.RegistrationError ¶ Bases: Exception Invalid or conflicting declarations, raised before the app serves. Events ¶ The events guide explains the two moments a handler runs in. A handler collection is listed on the application, or in an app's events entry of hinoki.toml . hinoki.events.Handlers ¶ Handlers ( name : str = '' ) A collection of event handlers, listed on the application to take effect. @handlers.in_transaction(Event) and @handlers.after_commit(Event) register the decorated function, which is returned unchanged so a test can call it directly. The event type is Event or, for events about one class, Event[Note] ; the handler's parameter must be annotated with the same type. Registration order is execution order. name instance-attribute ¶ name = name registrations property ¶ registrations : tuple [ Registration , ... ] in_transaction ¶ in_transaction ( kind : type [ E ], ) -> Callable [ [ Callable [[ E ], Awaitable [ None ]]], Callable [[ E ], Awaitable [ None ]], ] Run inside the transaction of the write that emitted the event. An exception or a timeout rolls the write back and reaches its caller. after_commit ¶ after_commit ( kind : type [ E ], ) -> Callable [ [ Callable [[ E ], Awaitable [ None ] | None ]], Callable [[ E ], Awaitable [ None ] | None ], ] Run after the outermost transaction commits (at once when none is open). A failure is logged and counted; it cancels nothing. hinoki.events.Created dataclass ¶ Created ( subject : type [ M ], instance : M ) A model row was inserted by insert ( acreate , asave of a new instance, abulk_create , generated CRUD create). instance is the stored instance. hinoki.events.Updated dataclass ¶ Updated ( subject : type [ M ], instance : M , changed : tuple [ str , ... ] ) A model instance was saved with changes ( asave , aupdate_from , abulk_update , generated CRUD update). changed names the columns that differed from the stored row before the write. hinoki.events.Deleted dataclass ¶ Deleted ( subject : type [ M ], count : int ) A DELETE statement removed count rows of the model ( adelete , abulk_delete , generated CRUD delete). No key or row is loaded. hinoki.events.emit async ¶ emit ( event : object ) -> None Emit event on the current worker's bus. hinoki.events.listener ¶ listener ( kind : type , subject : type | None = None ) -> EventBus | None The current bus when a write of subject (or, for an event with no subject, any emitter) must emit kind , else None : the guard of the emitting code paths (one context-variable read when no application bus is current). hinoki.events.Linked dataclass ¶ Linked ( subject : type [ M ], relation : str , key : object , targets : tuple [ object , ... ], ) Links were added to a many-to-many relation ( add or set of a LinkSet ). subject is the model that declares relation ; key is the primary key of the owner that was written (the declaring model, or the target when writing from the reverse side) and targets the keys of the rows now linked to it, in ascending order. Emitted only when something was added; needs after_commit handlers. hinoki.events.Unlinked dataclass ¶ Unlinked ( subject : type [ M ], relation : str , key : object , targets : tuple [ object , ... ], ) Links were removed from a many-to-many relation ( remove or set of a LinkSet ); the fields are those of Linked . Deleting a row that has links removes them without this event, like Deleted . Emitted only when something was removed; needs after_commit handlers. hinoki.events.AuthRejected dataclass ¶ AuthRejected ( reason : str , route : str , method : str ) A route's access policy refused a request (HTTP 401 or 403). reason is "missing" (no credentials), "invalid" (credentials the provider rejected) or "forbidden" (a caller without a required permission). route is the path template ( /notes/{note_id} ), never the requested path; method is the HTTP method, or WEBSOCKET . The payload holds no credential, caller, address or query string. Delivered through EventBus.notify , so it needs after_commit handlers. hinoki.events.RateLimited dataclass ¶ RateLimited ( policy : str , route : str , method : str , retry_after : int ) A route's rate-limit policy refused a request (HTTP 429). policy is the class name of the route's policy, retry_after the whole seconds the client was told to wait. The payload holds no key, caller, address or path. Delivered through EventBus.notify , so it needs after_commit handlers. hinoki.wsgi.WSGIAdapter ¶ WSGIAdapter ( app : Any ) start ¶ start () -> None Start the loop and the application's startup; safe to call twice. close ¶ close () -> None Run the application's shutdown and stop the loop; idempotent.

docs.text: Schemas ¶ hinoki.schema.Schema ¶ Base class for schemas. class PostCreate(Schema): title: str becomes a frozen, keyword-only dataclass. PostCreate.validate(data) checks decoded JSON strictly: no coercion, unknown keys refused by default, and every problem reported with its path. is_generic classmethod ¶ is_generic () -> bool True while type parameters are still open ( Envelope ). computed_fields classmethod ¶ computed_fields () -> dict [ str , ComputedSpec ] The read-only values this schema adds to its output, by name. apply_default classmethod ¶ apply_default ( name : str ) -> None Turn a Field(default_factory=...) attribute into a dataclass default. specs classmethod ¶ specs () -> dict [ str , FieldSpec ] Field descriptions, resolving forward references on first use. build_specs classmethod ¶ build_specs ( final : bool = False ) -> dict [ str , FieldSpec ] validate_normalizers classmethod ¶ validate_normalizers ( specs : dict [ str , FieldSpec ]) -> None Check that registered normalizers have a precise typed target. native_schema classmethod ¶ native_schema () -> core . CompiledSchema The Rust validator for this schema and everything it refers to, compiled on first use and cached on the class. validate_json classmethod ¶ validate_json ( raw : bytes ) -> Self | None The instance a JSON body describes, built by Rust in one pass, or None when the ordinary decode_json and validate must run on the same bytes (invalid input, or a schema with hooks or checks). validate classmethod ¶ validate ( data : object ) -> Self Build an instance from decoded JSON or raise ValidationError (validated in Rust). validate_text classmethod ¶ validate_text ( data : object ) -> Self Like validate for data that is all text, such as form fields ( {"count": ["2"]} ) or a parsed XML tree: text is first converted, in Rust, to the int , float and bool the fields declare. Anything that does not convert is left for validate to refuse. Before hooks see the raw text (each form value is a list of strings) and run first. fields classmethod ¶ fields () -> dict [ str , FieldSpec ] Immutable description shared by binding, docs and rules. to_dict ¶ to_dict ( * , exclude : Iterable [ str ] = ()) -> dict [ str , Any ] The field values as Python objects (UUID, datetime stay what they are), nested schemas converted too. Fields left UNSET are omitted, so the result is exactly "what the client sent" for a partial update. replace ¶ replace ( ** changes : Any ) -> Self A copy with changes (Python field names) applied. Every value is validated again, normalised and checked like a new instance, so the copy is as trustworthy as any other; fields that were never supplied stay unsupplied for dump(exclude_unset=True) . from_models classmethod ¶ from_models ( rows : Iterable [ object ], ** extra : Any ) -> list [ Self ] Build a list from a synchronous iterable of model rows. Each row follows from_model exactly. The iterable is consumed once, eagerly; this reads already-loaded attributes and never performs I/O. from_model classmethod ¶ from_model ( row : object , ** extra : Any ) -> Self Build this schema from a model instance: every field is read from the attribute of the same name, extra supplies or overrides values (for computed fields). Nested models become nested schemas. A field the row lacks is an error, and an unloaded relation still raises RelationNotLoaded : nothing here does I/O. dump ¶ dump ( * , include : Iterable [ str ] | None = None , exclude : Iterable [ str ] = (), exclude_unset : bool = False , by_alias : bool = True , ) -> dict [ str , Any ] Return JSON-compatible data with optional projection controls. server picks Kiso, Hinoki's Rust server (the default), or Granian. interface is how the server calls the target: asgi (a Hinoki application) or wsgi (a WSGI callable, such as a WSGIAdapter ); the --interface flag overrides it. access_log prints one line per request on either server; unset, hinoki dev logs and hinoki serve does not, and True or False decides for both. access_log_format (Rust server only: pretty , plain , json or logger ) chooses how a line looks; unset, it is pretty on a colour terminal and plain otherwise, and setting it turns the log on unless access_log is False . json writes one object per line with an RFC 3339 UTC time ; logger sends each to the hinoki.access logger. access_log_skip (Rust server only) lists paths the log leaves out, such as health checks: exact, or a prefix when the entry ends with * . access_log_slow_ms keeps only answers at least that slow. Both always keep failures (status 400 and up). recent_requests (Rust server only) is a file that also receives each record as JSON, for hinoki mcp 's recent_requests tool. server_timing (Rust server only) adds a Server-Timing header with the time taken and the serving lane: unset means in hinoki dev only. sighup (Rust server only; hinoki serve , where the system has SIGHUP ) says what the signal does: "reload" , which is also what unset means, replaces the workers one at a time with new processes that import the code and read the settings again, "stop" stops the server. reuse_port (Rust server only; Linux only, unset means automatic for multi-worker hinoki serve on a non-zero port) lets each worker bind its own SO_REUSEPORT socket instead of sharing one listening descriptor; False forces the shared descriptor everywhere. max_connections , header_read_timeout , body_read_timeout , write_timeout , native_dispatch and access_log_format , access_log_skip and access_log_slow_ms belong to the Rust server ( None keeps its default). hinoki serve refuses a setting the chosen server cannot honour. tls_cert_file and tls_key_file (PEM files, set together) serve HTTPS on either server; http2 adds HTTP/2 to it (ALPN h2 , TLS only, off by default). native_dispatch (unset means on) lets the Rust server run the async def handlers it can prove safe without an asyncio task; False Both always keep failures (status 400 and up). recent_requests (Rust server only) is a file that also receives each record as JSON, for hinoki mcp 's recent_requests tool. server_timing (Rust server only) adds a Server-Timing header with the time taken and the serving lane: unset means in hinoki dev only. sighup (Rust server only; hinoki serve , where the system has SIGHUP ) says what the signal does: "reload" , which is also what unset means, replaces the workers one at a time with new processes that import the code and read the settings again, "stop" stops the server. reuse_port (Rust server only; Linux only, unset means automatic for multi-worker hinoki serve on a non-zero port) lets each worker bind its own SO_REUSEPORT socket instead of sharing one listening descriptor; False forces the shared descriptor everywhere. max_connections , header_read_timeout , body_read_timeout , write_timeout , native_dispatch and access_log_format , access_log_skip and access_log_slow_ms belong to the Rust server ( None keeps its default). hinoki serve refuses a setting the chosen server cannot honour. tls_cert_file and tls_key_file (PEM files, set together) serve HTTPS on either server; http2 adds HTTP/2 to it (ALPN h2 , TLS only, off by default). native_dispatch (unset means on) lets the Rust server run the async def handlers it can prove safe without an asyncio task; False keeps every handler in one.

docs.text: CompressionSettings () Bases: Settings Response compression, done by Kiso only (it is ignored under another runner, and hinoki serve --server granian refuses enabled ). Off while enabled is false. encodings lists what the server offers in its order of preference ( br , gzip ). Bodies known to be smaller than min_size bytes, types outside types ( type/subtype , type/* or */*+suffix ) and responses with cache-control: no-transform are sent as they are. event_streams also compresses text/event-stream and files compresses file responses. gzip_level is 1 to 9, brotli_quality 0 to 9, and max_concurrent bounds the compressions in progress in one worker: past it, answers go out uncompressed.

docs.text: MetricsSettings () Bases: Settings Prometheus metrics, kept and served by Kiso only (they are ignored under another runner, and hinoki serve --server granian refuses listen ). Off while listen is unset. listen is the host:port of a dedicated listener (an IPv6 host goes in brackets) that serves only the exposition at path ; it never shares the application's port. A listener off the loopback needs allow (addresses or CIDRs of the peers that may scrape) or a token (the bearer token a scrape sends). buckets are the upper bounds, in seconds, of the duration histogram: 1 to 32 finite values, strictly increasing. With several workers each one writes a snapshot every snapshot_interval seconds and any worker's scrape reports them all, one series per worker label.

docs.text: EmailSettings () Bases: Settings Outbound email. backend has no default, so production never falls back to the console by accident: smtp delivers, console prints the rendered message (development) and memory keeps it in an outbox (tests). The SMTP fields apply to smtp only. port defaults to 587 for starttls , 465 for tls and 25 for none ; security="none" to a host off the loopback needs allow_insecure . username and password go together; read the password from a *_FILE variable. tls_ca_file adds PEM certificates to the bundled public roots (it does not replace them); certificates are always checked. default_sender is the From address of a message that sets none, and message_id_domain the domain of its Message-ID (default: the domain of default_sender , else helo_name , else localhost ). Durations are seconds, more than 0 and at most 3600: timeout bounds one whole send() including the wait for a connection and the retries, and must be at least connect_timeout . With check_on_startup the worker connects and authenticates while starting, and a failure aborts the start. memory_capacity bounds the outbox.

docs.text: Testing ¶ hinoki.testing.ASGIClient ¶ ASGIClient ( app : Hinoki , strict_errors : bool = False , * , host : str | None = None , ) Use as an async context manager so startup and shutdown always run. request async ¶ request ( method : str , path : str , * , json : Any = None , body : bytes = b "" , data : FormInput | None = None , files : FileInput | None = None , query : str = "" , headers : HeaderInput | None = None , token : str | None = None , max_bytes : int | None = MAX_BYTES , ) -> Response One request, including JSON or multipart test payloads. The whole response is collected; past max_bytes of body ( None : no limit) the client disconnects and raises BodyTooLarge , so an endless stream cannot hang a test (read one with client.stream() ). stream async ¶ stream ( method : str , path : str , ** options : Any ) -> AsyncIterator [ StreamReply ] A response read as it is produced. The head is available on entry; leaving the block disconnects the client, which ends the stream: async with client.stream("GET", "/events") as reply: async for piece in reply.chunks(): ... A server that runs ahead of the test waits for it (at most STREAM_PIECES pieces are buffered). check_declared ¶ check_declared ( method : str , path : str , reply : Response ) -> None With strict_errors=True : an error answer whose code the action did not declare ( errors=... ) and the framework does not produce by itself is an AssertionError . Catches business errors missing from OpenAPI. query async ¶ query ( path : str , ** options : Any ) -> Response An HTTP QUERY request ( json= is its body; the query= option is still the query string). hinoki.testing.SyncClient ¶ SyncClient ( app : Hinoki , timeout : float = 60.0 , * , host : str | None = None , ) The same client for tests written without async : the application runs on its own event loop in a background thread and every call blocks until the answer arrives (at most timeout seconds). with SyncClient(create_app()) as client: assert client.get("/health").status == 200 Use it only inside the with block. Sync model calls ( Model.get , create ) work inside the application's sync handlers, not in the test body itself: seed and inspect data with an async fixture or your own connection. stream ¶ stream ( method : str , path : str , ** options : Any ) -> Iterator [ SyncStreamReply ] ASGIClient.stream for tests without async : with client.stream("GET", "/events") as reply: first = next(reply.chunks()) hinoki.testing.ManualClock ¶ ManualClock ( start : datetime ) A thread-safe, controllable UTC clock for deterministic tests. set ¶ set ( value : datetime ) -> None Set the current instant; value must be timezone-aware. advance ¶ advance ( * , seconds : float = 0 ) -> datetime Advance by elapsed seconds and return the new UTC instant.

docs.text: Core API: application, routing and HTTP ¶ from hinoki import Hinoki, RouteGroup, Mount, http, errors and from hinoki.project import manifest_routes . Guides: function-based APIs , class-based APIs , register routes , errors . hinoki.app.Hinoki ¶ Hinoki ( * , settings : object | None = None , include : Sequence [ Includable ] | None = None , modules : Sequence [ Module | type [ Module ]] = (), commands : Sequence [ Command | type [ Command ]] = (), on_startup : Sequence [ Hook ] = (), on_shutdown : Sequence [ Hook ] = (), events : Sequence [ Handlers ] | None = None , email_templates : Sequence [ TemplateBase ] = (), startup_url : str | None = None , runtime : RuntimeConfig | None = None , title : str | None = None , version : str | None = None , openapi_url : str | Unset | None = UNSET , docs_url : str | Unset | None = UNSET , redoc_url : str | Unset | None = UNSET , llms_url : str | Unset | None = UNSET , openapi_version : Literal [ "3.1" , "3.2" ] | None = None , rules : RuleSet | None = None , enforce_rules : bool = True , waivers : str | Path | None = None , parsers : Sequence [ Parser ] | None = None , renderers : Sequence [ Renderer ] | None = None , middleware : Sequence [ Middleware ] | None = None , ) A Hinoki application. Registering routes builds the native router; nothing connects to anything, so factories returning Hinoki are safe to import and call. The instance is itself an ASGI callable ( granian --interface asgi module:app ); the first call freezes the declarations. on_startup and on_shutdown list functions taking the worker's ModuleContext ( async def or def ). Startup hooks run once per worker after the modules have started; shutdown hooks run before they are closed, and only after a startup that completed. events lists the Handlers collections whose typed event handlers run, in this order (see hinoki.events ); an unlisted one does nothing. email_templates lists the mail.Template objects the application sends. They go to the email module the email: EmailSettings field implies; with your own EmailModule pass them there instead. File templates are read and checked when each worker starts. startup_url optionally reserves a public GET/HEAD endpoint that returns {"status": "ok"} after worker startup. It reports startup completion, not application, database, or event-loop health. waivers names the owner's waiver file applied to the startup rules; it must exist. Without it, hinoki-rules.toml at the project root is used. settings instance-attribute ¶ settings = settings middleware instance-attribute ¶ middleware = check_middleware ( middleware ) waiver_file instance-attribute ¶ waiver_file : Path | None = ( None if waivers is None else Path ( waivers ) ) routes property ¶ routes : tuple [ Route , ... ] websockets property ¶ websockets : tuple [ WebSocketRoute , ... ] startup_url property ¶ startup_url : str | None The fixed startup-probe path, if one was configured. bindings property ¶ bindings : tuple [ Binding , ... ] modules property ¶ modules : tuple [ Module , ... ] commands property ¶ commands : tuple [ Command , ... ] The app's explicitly registered management commands. events property ¶ events : EventBus The typed event handlers listed in events= , fixed at construction. on_startup property ¶ on_startup : tuple [ Hook , ... ] Startup hooks, fixed when the application is constructed. on_shutdown property ¶ on_shutdown : tuple [ Hook , ... ] Shutdown hooks, fixed when the application is constructed. admin_settings ¶ admin_settings () -> AdminSettings | None The app's admin settings group, or None without built-in settings. now ¶ now ( clock : Clock = utc_now ) -> datetime Return an aware datetime in this application's configured timezone. settings_database ¶ settings_database ( declared : list [ Module ], ) -> DatabaseModule | None The database module implied by a database: DatabaseSettings field in the settings, unless the application declares its own. settings_email ¶ settings_email ( declared : list [ Module ], templates : Sequence [ TemplateBase ] = (), ) -> EmailModule | None The email module implied by an email: EmailSettings field in the settings, unless the application declares its own. templates go to the implied module; they are refused when there is none. module_of ¶ module_of ( module : Module | type [ Module ]) -> Module An instance as given, or a class built from this app's settings. include ¶ include ( * items : Includable ) -> None Register decorated functions, API subclasses and objects that expose an api() (the admin). Lists and tuples of those are flattened, so a feature package can export one routes list, and Mount(prefix, ...) places a feature under a path chosen here. All-or-nothing per call: on conflict the application is unchanged. lookup_websocket ¶ lookup_websocket ( path : str , ) -> tuple [ WebSocketRoute , dict [ str , str ]] | None The WebSocket action for a path, with its path parameters. routes_of staticmethod ¶ routes_of ( item : object ) -> list [ Route ] The routes an item declares: an API class, a decorated function, or an object exposing api() (the admin). inherited_parsers ¶ inherited_parsers ( route : Route ) -> tuple [ Parser , ... ] Parsers for an action without its own: the application's, unless an upload action needs multipart and they do not include it. with_defaults ¶ with_defaults ( route : Route ) -> Route The route with this application's default parsers/renderers filled in where the action did not choose its own. resolved_pagination ¶ resolved_pagination ( strategy : Pagination ) -> Pagination install ¶ install ( * modules : Module ) -> None Install modules and include their APIs. The whole graph (names, requirements, cycles) is validated here, so a broken graph fails in the factory, not in a worker. Nothing opens. lookup ¶ lookup ( method : str , path : str ) -> Found | MethodNotAllowed | None Distinguish a match, a wrong method and an unknown path. HEAD resolves through a matching GET route. Method-not-allowed results advertise HEAD whenever GET is available for the path. resolve ¶ resolve ( method : str , path : str ) -> tuple [ Route , dict [ str , str ]] | None Find the action for a request line; None if unknown or the method is not allowed (use lookup to tell them apart). openapi ¶ openapi () -> dict [ str , Any ] The OpenAPI document (3.2 by default, 3.1 with openapi_version ). asgi ¶ asgi () -> ASGIAdapter The ASGI adapter for this worker; builds and validates bindings once. enforce ¶ enforce () -> None Fail with every startup-rule violation when rules are enforced. With enforce_rules=False the diagnostics are only logged. The owner's waivers apply as in hinoki check : waivers= when given, else the project's hinoki-rules.toml . An invalid waiver file always fails. error_handler ¶ error_handler ( kind : type [ Exception ]) -> ErrorRegistrar Decorator: answer kind with a function of the exception that returns the APIError to send. It returns the function unchanged. @app.error_handler(stripe.CardError) def card_error(error: stripe.CardError) -> errors.APIError: return errors.APIError(error.user_message, status=402) Errors that already are APIError subclasses need no handler. hinoki.api.API ¶ Base class for a resource: several methods, standard or custom. class Posts(API, path='/posts') . Instances hold no per-request state; methods declared with @http.get / @http.post /... become actions. prefix class-attribute ¶ prefix : str = '' routes classmethod ¶ routes () -> list [ Route ] Routes of this class with the prefix applied, in definition order. Members are resolved by name, most derived class first, so an override without a decorator removes the inherited route. websockets classmethod ¶ websockets () -> list [ WebSocketRoute ] @http.websocket methods with the prefix applied, in definition order; the class is created without arguments for each connection. member_names classmethod ¶ member_names () -> list [ str ] Member names, most derived class first, so an override without a decorator removes the inherited action. declared_route classmethod ¶ declared_route ( name : str , member : object ) -> Route | None mount classmethod ¶ mount ( route : Route ) -> Route mounted_path classmethod ¶ mounted_path ( path : str ) -> str hinoki.routing.RouteGroup ¶ RouteGroup ( prefix : str = "" , * , access : Access | None = None , atomic : bool = False , errors : Sequence [ type [ APIError ]] = (), cors : Cors | None = None , include_in_schema : bool = True , tags : Sequence [ str ] = (), ) A function-based route group with a shared path prefix and defaults. Decorated functions belong to this group and the group can be included once in a Hinoki application. Use API for class-based resources. tasks = RouteGroup("/tasks", access=member_only, atomic=True, errors=(NotFound,)) @tasks.get("/") # GET /tasks async def listing(...): ... @tasks.post("/", status=201) # POST /tasks, atomic=True async def create(...): ... @tasks.get("/health", access=None) # public on purpose, overriding the group prefix is prepended to every path ( "/" means the prefix itself), access is the default policy (pass access=None on an action to make it public), atomic=True makes POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE transactional unless the action says atomic=False , errors are added to each action's own and cors is the default http.Cors ( cors=None on an action keeps the application's policy). include_in_schema=False leaves every action out of the OpenAPI document unless it says include_in_schema=True , and tags come before the tags of each action. The result is an ordinary action: rules, OpenAPI and the MCP see no difference. prefix instance-attribute ¶ prefix = prefix access instance-attribute ¶ access = access atomic instance-attribute ¶ atomic = atomic errors instance-attribute ¶ errors = tuple ( errors ) cors instance-attribute ¶ cors = check_cors ( cors ) include_in_schema instance-attribute ¶ include_in_schema = check_flag ( "include_in_schema" , include_in_schema ) tags instance-attribute ¶ tags = check_tags ( tags ) handlers property ¶ handlers : tuple [ Callable [ ... , object ], ... ] The decorated handlers in declaration order. declare ¶ declare ( method : str , path : str , options : dict [ str , Any ] ) -> RouteDeclaration get ¶ get ( path : str , ** options : Unpack [ GroupActionOptions ] ) -> _GroupRouteDeclaration post ¶ post ( path : str , ** options : Unpack [ GroupActionOptions ] ) -> _GroupRouteDeclaration put ¶ put ( path : str , ** options : Unpack [ GroupActionOptions ] ) -> _GroupRouteDeclaration patch ¶ patch ( path : str , ** options : Unpack [ GroupActionOptions ] ) -> _GroupRouteDeclaration delete ¶ delete ( path : str , ** options : Unpack [ GroupActionOptions ] ) -> _GroupRouteDeclaration query ¶ query ( path : str , ** options : Unpack [ GroupActionOptions ] ) -> _GroupRouteDeclaration hinoki.routing.Includable ¶ Includable = ( type [ API ] | Callable [ ... , object ] | RouteGroup | Mount | ExposesRoutes | Sequence [ Includable ] ) What Hinoki(include=[...]) and app.include(...) accept: an API class, a decorated function, a RouteGroup , a Mount , an object with api() (the admin) or a list or tuple of those. hinoki.routing.Mount ¶ Mount ( prefix : str , * items : object ) Places routes under a path prefix chosen where the application is declared. Hinoki(include=[ health, Mount("/tasks", tasks.routes), Mount("/billing", billing.routes), ]) The feature keeps paths relative to itself ( / and /{id} ) and the root declaration shows where each feature lives. Items are anything include accepts, including lists and other mounts; prefixes join outside in. prefix instance-attribute ¶ prefix = prefix items instance-attribute ¶ items = items hinoki.project.manifest_routes ¶ manifest_routes ( start : Path | None = None , ) -> list [ Includable ] The routes [project] routes declares in hinoki.toml (or [] when omitted). The manifest is found from start , by default the directory of the calling file (the working directory when the caller has no file), upwards. Outside a project this raises ProjectError . hinoki.project.manifest_events ¶ manifest_events ( start : Path | None = None , ) -> list [ Handlers ] The Handlers each app of hinoki.toml declares, in dependency order, for Hinoki(events=manifest_events()) . The manifest is found as for manifest_routes ; outside a project this raises ProjectError . hinoki.project.manifest_middleware ¶ manifest_middleware ( start : Path | None = None , ) -> list [ Middleware ] The [project] middleware list of hinoki.toml , flattened in listed order (the first listed runs outermost), for Hinoki(middleware=manifest_middleware()) . The manifest is found as for manifest_routes ; outside a project this raises ProjectError . hinoki.project.manifest_rules ¶ manifest_rules ( start : Path | None = None ) -> RuleSet The [project] rules list of hinoki.toml merged, in listed order, into one RuleSet for Hinoki(rules=manifest_rules()) . The manifest is found as for manifest_routes ; outside a project this raises ProjectError . Hinoki() loads the routes, events, middleware and rules of hinoki.toml by itself; call these functions only to pass the same lists by hand. For model-backed route generation, see Generate CRUD routes and the CRUD API reference . POST property ¶ POST : QueryDict Form fields; empty when the body is not a form. FILES property ¶ FILES : MultiDict [ UploadedFile ] Uploaded files of a multipart body; empty otherwise. parsed ¶ parsed () -> Parsed The body through the parser for its content type, once; raises InvalidBody (415 for an unlisted type, 400 for a malformed body). accepts_form ¶ accepts_form () -> bool hinoki.http.response.Response ¶ Response ( status : int = 200 , body : bytes | str = b "" , headers : ResponseHeaders = (), content_type : str | None = None , ) Status, headers and body chosen by the handler. status instance-attribute ¶ status = status body instance-attribute ¶ body = raw headers instance-attribute ¶ headers = [ encode_header ( name , value ) for name , value in items ] raw classmethod ¶ raw ( status : int , body : bytes , headers : Sequence [ tuple [ bytes , bytes ]], ) -> Response A response from encoded parts, checked like one built from text: a framing or server header, a bad name or a CR/LF in a value raise ValueError .
